Abanteus.definition: Abantēus adj., of Abas (king of Argos): Argi, O.

Abantiades.definition: Abantiadēs ae, m a son or descendant of Abas (king of Argos), O.

Abdera.definition: Abdēra ōrum, n a town of Thrace, proverbial for narrow-minded people, C., L.

Abella.definition: Abella ae, f a town of Campania, V.

Aborigines.definition: Aborīginēs um, m ab + origo, the first ancestors of the Romans, L., S.

Abydenus.definition: Abȳdēnus adj., of Abydus, a town in Mysia: aqua, O.

Academia.definition: Acadēmīa ae, f the gymnasium near Athens, where Plato taught. — Meton., the doctrines of Plato, the Academic philosophy; the philosophers of the Academy; a place near Puteoli, where Cicero wrote the Academica; Cicero'…

Academica.definition: Acadēmica ōrum, n the title of Cicero's treatise on the Academic philosophy.

Academicus1.definition: Acadēmicus adj., of the Academy, Academic: libri, i. e. Academica.— As subst:

Academicus2.definition: Acadēmicus ī, m an Academic philosopher;

Academus.definition: Acadēmus ī, m a mythical hero of Athens: silvae Academi, i. e. Academia, H.

Acarnanicus.definition: Acarnānicus adj., of Acarnania (a country of western Greece): coniuratio, L.

Acbarus.definition: Acbarus (Agbarus) ī, m the local title of the Arabian kings of Edessa: rex Arabum, Ta.

Accianus.definition: Acciānus adj. Accius, of the poet Lu. Accius.

Achaei.definition: Achaeī ōrum, m the inhabitants of the district of Achaia.

Achaemenes.definition: Achaemenēs īs, m, *a)xaime/nhs, an ancestor of the kings of Persia: dives, H.

Achaemenius.definition: 'Achaemenius adj. Achaemenes, Persian, Parthian: urbes, O.: costum, H.'

Achaias.definition: Achāias (poet. Achāïas, quadrisyl.), adis, f a Greek woman, O.

Achaicus.definition: Achāicus adj., Achaean, Grecian: manus, V.: ignis, H.: homines.

Achais.definition: Achāis idis or idos, adj.,f Grecian: urbes, O.—As subst. for Achaia, Greece, O.

Achaius.definition: Achāius adj., Grecian: castra, V., O.

Acharnanus.definition: Acharnānus adj., of Acharnae (an Attic deme), N.

Acheloius.definition: Achelōius adj., of the river Achelous: pocula, fresh water, V.: Callirhoë , daughter of Achelous, O.

Acheron.definition: Acherōn tis, m (V., H.), *a)xe/rwn, a river of the lower world.— Hence, the infernal regions, V.

Acheruns.definition: Acherūns untis, m or f (C., N.), *a)xe/rwn, a river of the lower world.— Hence, the infernal regions, V.

Acherusius.definition: Acherūsīus (-ūnsius) adj., of the Acheron in Bruttium: aqua, L.—Of the under-world, Enn. ap. C.

Achilles.definition: Achillēs is (poet. also eī or ī; acc. ea; voc. e; abl. ī ), m, *a)xilleu/s, a Grecian hero.

Achilleus.definition: Achillēus adj., of Achilles, V., O.

Achivus.definition: Achīvus adj., Achaean, Grecian, O.—Plur. as subst, the Greeks.

Acidalia.definition: Acīdalia ae, f an epithet of Venus, from the fountain Acidalia in Boeotia, V.

Acrisioneus.definition: Acrisiōnēus adj., of Acrisius, V., O.

Acrisioniades.definition: Ācrisiōniadēs ae, n a descendant of Acrisius, i. e. Perseus, O.

Acrisius.definition: Ācrisius ī, m a king of Argos, V., O.

Acroceraunia.definition: Acroceraunia ōrum, n, ta *a)krokerau/nia, a rocky promontory of Epirus, H., O.

Actaei.definition: Actaeī ōrum, m the people of Attica, N.

Actaeon.definition: Actaeōn onis, m, *a)ktai/wn, grandson of Cadmus, O.

Actaeus.definition: Actaeus adj., prop. of Acte (the coast of Attica).—Hence, Attic, Athenian, V., O.—Subst plur.,

Actiacus.definition: 'Actiacus adj., of Actium: Phoebus, worshipped at Actium, O.'

Actias.definition: Actias adis, adj., f, *a)ktia/s, Athenian, V.

Actium.definition: Actium ī, n, *a)/ktion, a promontory of Acarnania, C., L.

Actius.definition: 'Actius adj., of Actium: ludi, V., H.'

Adelphi.definition: Adelphī ōrum, *a)delfoi/, The Brothers (a comedy), T.

Adonis.definition: Adōnis is (dat. Adōnidī, C.; voc. Adōni, O.), m a youth beloved by Venus, V.

Aegaeus.definition: Aegaeus adj., Aegean: mare, aequor, the Aegean sea, Grecian archipelago, V., O.—As subst n., the Aegean sea.

Aegyptius.definition: Aegyptius adj., Egyptian, C., N.—As subst, an Egyptian, Cs., C.

Aeneius.definition: Aenēius adj. Aeneas, of Aeneas, V., O.

Aeolius.definition: Aeolius adj. 1. Of Aeolus, the god of the winds: venti, Tb.: virgo, i. e. Arne or Canace.— 2. Of the Aeolians: puella, i. e. Sappho, H.: lyra, O.: plectrum, Pr.

Aesopius.definition: Aesōpius adj. Aesopus, Aesopian: fabulae, like Aesop's, Ph.

Aethiops.definition: Aethiops opis, m, *ai)qi/oy (burnt-face), an Ethiopian, negro: stipes, a blockhead of a negro. —Adj., Ethiopian: lacūs (plur.), O.

Afer.definition: Āfer Āfra, Āfrum, adj., African. — As subst, m., an African: dirus, i. e. Hannibal, H.: te Afris praeficere: discincti, V.

Africa.definition: Āfrica ae, f a Carthaginian word, Libya, the Carthaginian territory, C., S.; the province of Africa, C.—Africa (the continent), S.

Africanus.definition: Āfricānus adj. Africa, of Africa, African: bellum: possessiones, N. — Plur f. as subst., arum (sc. ferae), panthers, L.

Africus.definition: Āfricus adj. Africa, African: terra: procellae, i. e. from the southwest, H. — As subst, m. (sc. ventus), the southwest wind, V., H.

Agenor.definition: Agēnor oris, m a king of Phoenicia: Agenoris urbs, i. e. Carthage, V.— Agenore natus, i. e. Cadmus, O.

Agonalis.definition: Agōnālis e, adj., of the festival Agonalia (in honor of Janus, on Jan. 9th): lux, O.

Agyieus.definition: Agyīeus —, voc. Agyīeu (trisyl.), an epithet of Apollo, as guardian of streets, H.

Aius.definition: Āius ī, m aio, the speaker; in full, Aius Locutius, L., or Aius Loquens, C.; a deity supposed to have notified the Romans of a coming invasion by the Gauls.

Alauda.definition: Alauda ae, m Celtic, a soldier of the legion Alauda (lark), which Caesar raised in Gaul, C.

Albula.definition: Albula ae, f old name of the Tiber, V., O.

Alcides.definition: Alcīdēs ae, m a descendant of Alceus; esp. his grandson Hercules, V., H.

Alcinous.definition: Alcinous ī, m a king of the Phaeacians: iuventus Alcinoi, i. e. voluptuaries, H.: Alcinoi silvae, i. e. fruit-trees, V.

Alecto.definition: Ālectō (All-) —, acc. tō, f, *a)lhktw/, one of the three furies (only nom. and acc.), V.

Alliensis.definition: Alliēnsis e, adj. Allia, of the river Allia (where the Romans were defeated by the Gauls): dies, the battle day of Allia (July 18, a dies nefastus), C., L.

Allifanus.definition: Allīfānus adj., of Allifae (a town of Samnium): ager. — Plur n. as subst, large drinkingcups made at Allifae, H.

Allobrox.definition: Allobrox ogis, acc. oga, m one of the Allobroges, a warlike people of Gaul.— Meton., a barbarian, Iu.

Alpinus.definition: Alpīnus adj. Alpes, of the Alps, Alpine: rigor, O.: nives, V.: gentes, L.

Alyattes.definition: Alyattēs eī, m, *a)lua/tths, a king of Lydia, father of Croesus: regnum Alyattei, H.

Amaryllis.definition: Amaryllis idis or idos, f acc. Amaryllida; voc. Amarylli, *a)marulli/s, a shepherdess, V.

Amathusia.definition: Amathūsia ae, f Venus (worshipped at Amathus in Cyprus), Ct., O.

Amazon.definition: Amāzōn onis, f Scythian, an Amazon.— Plur., Amazons, a tribe of warlike women on the river Thermodon: Threiciae, V.: exsultat Amazon, V.

Amazonis.definition: Amāzonis idis, f an Amazon, V.

Ambiorix.definition: Ambiorīx īgis, m a chief of the Eburones, Cs.

Ambracia.definition: Ambracia ae, f a town of Epirus, Cs., L., O.

Amerinus.definition: Amerīnus adj. Ameria, of Ameria (in Umbria): municeps retinacula, willow twigs for tying up vines, V.

Aminaeus.definition: Amīnaeus (-ēus) adj., of Aminaea, a town of the Piceni: vites, a favorite kind of vine, V.

Amphictyones.definition: Amphictyones um, m the assembly of the confederated Greek States, Amphictyons, C., Ta.

Amphion.definition: Amphīōn onis, m, *a)mfi/wn, a son of Jupiter, V., H., O.

Amphrysius.definition: Amphrȳsius adj., of Amphrysus.—Poet., of Apollo: vates, the Sibyl, V.

Amphrysus.definition: Amphrȳsus or Amphrȳsos ī, m, *a)mfruso/s, a small river of Thessaly, V., O.

Ampsanctus.definition: Ampsānctus (Am-) ī, m see ambi-, all hallowed (sc. lacus), a lake of Italy, noted for pestiferous exhalations.—Poet.: valles (of the entrance to the infernal regions), V.

Amyclae.definition: Amȳclae ārum, f, *a)mu/klai. I. A town of Laconia, O.—II. A town of Latium, V.

Amyclaeus.definition: Amȳclaeus Amyclae, I., of Amyclae, Laconian, V.

Anagninus.definition: Anāgnīnus adj., of Anagnia (a town of Latium).—Subst: Anagninum, an estate near Anagnia.

Anchises.definition: Anchīsēs ae (abl. Anchisā, V.), m, *agxi/shs, father of Aeneas, V., O.

Anchiseus.definition: Anchīsēus adj. Anchises, of Anchises, V.

Anchisiades.definition: Anchīsiadēs ae, m patr., son of Anchises Aeneas, V.

Anguitenens.definition: Anguitenēns entis, m anguis + teneo, serpent-holder, the constellation Serpent-bearer, C.

Aniensis.definition: Aniēnsis e (C., L.), or Aniēnus (V.), adj. Anio, of the Anio.

Anio.definition: Aniō ēnis, m a tributary of the Tiber, V., H., C.

Antecanem.definition: Ante-canem m, transl. of *proku/wn, Procyon, the forerunner of the dog (Sirius), lesser dog-star.

Antoniaster.definition: Antōniaster trī, m a servile imitator of the orator Antonius.

Antonius.definition: Antōnius a gentile name.—As adj., of the triumvir Antonius: leges.

Apollinaris.definition: Apollināris e, adj. Apollo, of Apollo, sacred to Apollo: laurea, H.: aedes, L.: ludi, in honor of Apollo.

Apollo.definition: Apollō inis, mApollo.—Poet.: nautis aperitur Apollo, i. e. the temple of Apollo, V.

Appenninicola.definition: Appennīnicola ae, m COL-, an inhabitant of the Apennines, V.

Appenninigena.definition: Appennīnigena ae, adj. GEN-: Thybris, born on the Apennines, O.

Appius.definition: Appius ī, m a family name in the gens Claudia. — As adj., Appian: via, the Appian Way, from Rome to Capua. — Called Appia via, H.: Appia, H., C.

Aprilis.definition: Aprīlis is, adj. aperio, of April: mensis: Nonae.—As subst, April, O.

Aquinas.definition: Aquīnās ātis, adj., of Aquinum: fucus, H.

Arabs.definition: Arabs abis, adj., Arabian. — Plur., the Arabs.

Arateus.definition: Arātēus (Arātī-) adj., of the poet Aratus: carmina.

Arcadicus.definition: Arcadicus adj., Arcadian: urbs, L. — Meton., rustic, stupid: iuvenis, Iu.

Arcas.definition: Arcas adis (ados, O.), adj., Arcadian: rex, Evander, V.—As subst, an Arcadian, C., O.

Archiacus.definition: 'Archiacus adj., made by Archias (a cabinetmaker); hence, cheap, common: lecti, H.'

Archilochius.definition: Archilochīus adj., like Archilochus.—Hence, severe: edicta.

Arcitenens.definition: Arcitenēns (Arquit-) ntis, adj. arcus + teneo, holding a bow, bow-bearing: deus, Apollo. —As subst: Apollo, V.—As a constellation, the Archer.

Arctos.definition: Arctos ī (acc. Arcton, V., O.), f the Great Bear (Ursa Major): geminae, the two Bears, O.: gelidae, V.: Arcton excipere, to be exposed to, look towards, the north, H.

Areopagus.definition: Arēopagus (Arīo-) ī, m Mars' Hill at Athens, on which the highest court sat.

Argi.definition: Argī orum, m Argos, the Argives, Greeks, V.

Armilustrum.definition: Armilustrum ī, n a place in Rome, where the festival Armilustrium (consecration of arms) was celebrated, L.

Armoricae.definition: Armoricae (Arem-) ārum, f adj. Celtic, maritime: civitates, of northwestern Gaul, Cs.

Atabulus.definition: Atābulus ī, m the southeast wind, Sirocco, H.

Atellanus.definition: Ātellānus adj., of Atella (a town of Campania), C.: fabella, a kind of farce, first exhibited at Atella, L.—As subst f., a comic farce, L.

Athenae.definition: Athēnae ārum, f, *a)thh=nai, Athens, C., L., H., O.

Atrides.definition: Atrīdēs ae (voc. -da, H.; -dē, H.), m patr., son of Atreus.

Attalicus.definition: 'Attalicus adj. Attalus, of Attalus (king of Pergamus): condiciones, i. e. rich, H.'

Augustus2.definition: Augustus ī, m 1 Augustus, a cognomen given to Octavius Caesar as emperor, his majesty. —Hence, As adj., of Augustus, of the emperor, imperial: caput, O.: mensis, the month of August (Sextilis), Iu.

Avernalis.definition: Avernālis e, adj. Avernus, of Lake Avernus: aquae, H.: nymphae, O.: Sibylla, Pr.

Avernus.definition: Avernus adj., a)/ornos (prop., birdless, because its exhalations destroyed life). — Hence (with or without lacus): Avernus, a lake near Cumae, the fabled entrance to the lower world, C., V., L.—Of Lake Avernus: freta,…

abactus.definition: abāctus P. of abigo, driven away, driven off: nox abacta, driven back (from the pole), i. e. already turned towards dawn, V.: abacta nullā conscientiā , restrained by, H.

abacus.definition: abacus ī, m a table of precious material for the display of plate, C.; luv.

abalienatio.definition: abaliēnātiō īnis, f abalieno, in law, a transfer of property, sale, cession, C.

abalieno.definition: ab-aliēnō āvī, ātus, āre, to convey away, make a former transfer of, sell, alienate: agros vectigalīs populi R.: pecus.— Fig., to separate, remove, abstract: ab sensu rerum animos, abstracted their thoughts from, L.: …

abavus.definition: abavus ī, m 1 AV-, a grandfather's grandfather, C.; an ancestor (rare), C.

abdicatio.definition: abdicātiō ōnis, f 1. abdico, a formal laying down, voluntary renunciation, abdication: dictaturae, L.

abdico1.definition: ab-dicō āvī, ātus, āre, to disown, disavow, reject: ubi plus mali quam boni reperio, id totum abdico atque eicio: abdicari Philippum patrem, Cu.—With se and abl, to give up an office before the legal term expires, res…

abdico2.definition: ab-dīcō dīxī, —, ere, in augury, to forbid by an unfavorable omen, reject (opp. addico), C.

abditus.definition: abditus adj. P. of abdo, hidden, concealed, secret: virgo, locked up, H.: sub terram: ne ea omnia ... ita abdita latuisse videantur, ut, etc., hidden beyond discovery: copias abditas constituunt, in ambush, Cs.: secre…

abdo.definition: ab-dō idī, itus, ere 2. do, to put away, remove, set aside: impedimenta in silvas, Cs.; often with se, to go away, betake oneself: se in contrariam partem terrarum: se in Menapios, to depart, Cs.: se domum. — Praegn.,…

abdomen.definition: abdōmen inis, n the belly, abdomen: abdomine tardus, unwieldy, Iuv.— Fig., gluttony, greed: insaturabile: abdominis voluptates.

abduco.definition: ab-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere (imper. sometimes abdū ce, T.), to lead away, take away, carry off, remove, lead aside: filiam abduxit suam, has taken away (from her husband), T.: cohortes secum, Cs.: squalent abductis arva…

abeo.definition: ab-eō iī, itūrus, īre (abin' for abisne, T.), to go from, go away, go off, go forth, go, depart: ab urbe: ex eorum agris: ex conspectu, out of sight, Cs.: mater abit templo, O.: abire fugā, to flee, V.: in angulum ali…

abequito.definition: ab-equitō āvī, —, āre, to ride away (once): Syracusas, L.

aberratio.definition: aberrātiō ōnis, f aberro, a relief, diversion (rare): a dolore, a molestiis.

aberro.definition: ab-errō āvī, —, āre, to wander out of the way, lose the way, go astray: taurus, qui pecore aberrasset, L.—Fig., in word or deed, to go astray, wander: sed tamen aberro, find diversion; (usu. with ab, to miss): a propo…

abhinc.definition: ab-hinc adv. of time, ago, since, before now, usu. with acc. of duration: abhinc mensīs decem fere, T., C., H.; very rarely with abl: comitiis iam abhinc diebus triginta factis, i. e. before that time: quo tempore? ab…

abhorrens.definition: abhorrēns ntis, adj. P. of abhorreo, incongruous, inappropriate: vestrae istae lacrimae, L.: oratio.

abhorreo.definition: ab-horreō uī, —, ēre, to shrink back from, have an aversion for, shudder at, abhor: omnes aspernabantur, omnes abhorrebant, shrank (from him). — In weakened sense, to be averse, be disinclined to, not to wish: a nupti…

abicio.definition: abiciō (a usu. long by position) or abiiciō iēcī, iectus, ere ab + iacio, to throw from one, cast away, throw away, throw down: abiecit hastas, has given up the fight: in proelio ... scutum: arma, Cs.: se ad pedes: eg…

abiecte.definition: abiectē adv. with comp. abiectus, dispiritedly, abjectly: casum et dolorem ferre; lowly, meanly: quo abiectius nati sunt, etc., Ta.

abiectio.definition: abiectiō ōnis, f abicio, a casting down; only fig.: debilitatio atque abiectio animi.

abiectus.definition: abiectus adj. with comp. P. of abicio, low, crouching: in herbis olor, i. e. dying, O.—Fig., of speech, low, common, without elevation: verba.— Of rank or station, low, common, mean: familia abiecta atque obscura.—Cas…

abiegnus.definition: abiēgnus adj. abies + GEN-, of fir-wood, deal: trabes, Her.: equus, i. e. the wooden horse before Troy, Pr.: hastile, L.

abies.definition: abiēs etis, f (poet. abl. abiete, trisyl.,abl. abietibus, quadrisyl.), the fir-tree, silver-fir: nigra, V.: enodis, O.: patriae, V.—Esp., the wood of the firtree, fir, deal: sectā, V.—Meton., something made of fir, a …

abigo.definition: abigō ēgī, āctus, ere ab+ago, to drive away, drive off: alqm rus, T.: mercatorem, H.: muscas. —Esp. of cattle, etc., to drive away (as plunder), carry off: pecus: partum sibi medicamentis, to force a birth.— Fig., to …

abitio.definition: abitiō ōnis, f abeo, a departure, T.

abitus.definition: abitus ūs, m abeo, a departure, removal: post abitum huius pestis: excruciarier eius abitu, T.—An outlet, way of exit, passage out: abitum custode coronant, V.: vehicula sepserant abitūs, Ta.

abiudico.definition: ab-iūdicō āvī, ātus, āre, of a judge or tribunal, to give judgment against, deprive by a judicial decision, adjudge away: ob iniuriam agri abiudicati, i. e. taking away their land by an unjust decision, L.: res ab ali…

abiungo.definition: ab-iungō iūnxī, iūnctus, ere, to unyoke, loose from harness: iuvencum, V. — Fig., to remove, part: abiuncto Labieno vehementer timebat, was apprehensive for Labienus, cut off from him, Cs.

abiuro.definition: ab-iūrō āvī, ātus, āre, to deny on oath, abjure: creditum, S.: abiuratae rapinae, V.

ablegatio.definition: ablēgātiō ōnis, f ablēgo, a sending away, sending off (rare): iuventutis ad bellum, L.

ablego.definition: ab-lēgō āvī, ātus, āre, to send off, send out of the way, banish, send into exile: aliquo mihist hinc ablegandus, T.: ab urbe, L.: a fratris adventu me ablegat, i. e. prevents me from being present: magna pars ablegat…

abligurrio.definition: ab-ligurriō (-ūriō) īvī, —, īre, to consume in dainty living, waste in feasting (rare): patria bona, T.

abludo.definition: ab-lūdō —, ere, to play out of tune.—Fig. (once): haec a te non multum abludit imago, is not very unlike your case, H.

abluo.definition: ab-luō luī, lūtus, ere, to wash away, remove by washing: Aeneae quaecumque obnoxia morti, all that is mortal, O.: ablutā caede, blood, V.— Fig.: perturbatio animi placatione abluatur, removed by propitiation: periuria…

abnego.definition: ab-negō āvī, ātus, āre, to refuse, deny (poet.): tibi coniugium, V.: nec comitem abnegat (sc. se). H.: nummos, deny receipt of, Iu.: medicas adhibere manūs ad volnera, V.: Abnegat inceptoque haeret, refuses and abides…

abnormis.definition: abnōrmis e, adj. ab+norma, deviating from rule, irregular (once): abnormis sapiens crassāque Minervā, i. e. of no school, H.

abnuo.definition: ab-nuō nuī, nuitūrus, ere, to refuse by a sign, deny, refuse, reject, decline: plebs abnuit dilectum, L.: regi pacem, S.: nihil studio meo: imperium, refuse obedience to, L.: omen, not to accept, V.: linguam Romanam, …

abnuto.definition: abnūtō —, —, āre, intens. abnuo, to forbid with emphasis (old): quid te adirier abnutas, i. e. forbid approach to thee, Enn. ap. C.

aboleo.definition: aboleō olēvī, olitus, ēre 2 OL-, to destroy, abolish, efface, put out of the way, annihilate: magistratum alicui, L.: nefandi viri monumenta, V.: dedecus armis, V.; of animals dead of the plague: viscera undis, to des…

abolesco.definition: abolēscō olēvī, —, ere, incept. aboleo, to decay gradually, vanish, disappear, die out: nomen vetustate, L.: tanti gratia facti, V.

abolitio.definition: abolitiō ōnis, f aboleo, an abolition: tributorum, Ta.— An annulling: sententiae, Ta.

abolla.definition: 'abolla ae, f a mantle, cloak, Iu.; (prov.): facinus maioris abollae, of higher grade, Iu.'

abominor.definition: ab-ōminor ātus, ārī, dep. orig. of bad omens, to deprecate, wish to nullify: quod abominor, which may God avert! O.: bene facitis, quod abominamini, you do well to deprecate it. L. — Meton., to abhor, detest, execrate…

abortio.definition: abortiō ōnis, f the procuring of an untimely birth, abortion: merces abortionis.

abortivus.definition: abortīvus adj., prematurely born: Sisyphus, H.—Neutr. plur. as subst, premature births, Iu. — Meton., that which causes abortion: abortivum, Iu.

abortus.definition: abortus ūs, m an untimely birth, T., C.
