acinus.definition: acinus ī, m, (acina, ae, f, Ct.), a small berry: acini vinaceus, a grape-stone: aridum, H.

acipenser.definition: acipēnser eris, m 2 AC- + pinna, a sea-fish, (esteemed a dainty dish), C., H., O.

aclys.definition: āclys (āclis) ydis, f a small javelin with a strap, V.

acoenonoetus.definition: acoenonoētus ī, m, a)koinono/htos, without common-sense, Iu.

aconitum.definition: aconītum (-ton) ī, n a poisonous plant, wolf's-bane, aconite, O., V.—Poet., poison: lurida, O.

acratophoron.definition: acrātophoron (-um) ī, n, a)kratofo/ron, a vessel for unmixed wine.

acredula.definition: acrēdula ae, f an unknown animal.

acriculus.definition: ācriculus adj. dim. 2 ācer, irritable: senex.

acrimonia.definition: ācrimōnia ae, f 2 ācer, sharpness, pungency; only fig., severity, acrimony, energy: ad resistendum: causae.

acriter.definition: ācriter adv. with comp. ācrius, and sup. ācerrimē 2 ācer, sharply, fiercely: caedunt acerrime: maleficium vindicare.—Fig., of the sight, keenly: intueri.—Of the mind, keenly, sharply, accurately: intellegere: acrius v…

acroama.definition: acroāma atis, n, a)kro/ama, an entertainment for the ear; meton., a reader, musician, storyteller, buffoon: actor et acroama: acroama audire.

acroasis.definition: acroāsis is, f, a)kro/asis, prop., a hearing; hence, a discourse, lecture, C.

acta.definition: acta ae, f, a)kth/, the sea-shore, sea-beach: in actā iacere: in solā actā, V.—Meton., plur, a holiday, life of ease (at the sea-shore): eius.

actio.definition: āctiō ōnis, f 1 AG-, a putting in motion; hence, a performing, doing, action: virtutis laus in actione consistit, in deeds.—Esp.: gratiarum, a rendering.—Of an orator or player, a rendering, declamation: consulis. — P…

actito.definition: āctitō āvī, —, āre, freq. ago, to conduct often, be engaged in, act in: causas: tragoedias.

actor.definition: āctor ōris, m 1 AG-, a driver: pecoris, a shepherd, O. — An agent, doer, performer, actor: hunc actorem auctoremque habebant, worker and counsellor, N.: orator verborum, actorque rerum: publicus, manager of public pro…

actuaria.definition: āctuāria ae, f actuarius; sc. navis, a swift boat.

actuariola.definition: āctuāriola ae, f dim. actuaria, a row-boat, barge.

actuarius.definition: āctuārius adj. ago, easily driven, swift: navigia, Cs.: naves, L.

actum.definition: āctum ī, n P. of ago, a deed, transaction, proposition, decree, law: alcuius: acta Caesaris. —Plur., ācta, a register of public events, records, journal: ex actis alqd cognosse.

actuosus.definition: āctuōsus adj. ago, full of life, active: partes (orationis): virtus.

actus2.definition: āctus ūs, m 1 AG-, a driving, impulse, setting in motion: actu inflectit feram: Fertur magno mons actu, with a mighty impulse, V. — Meton., a right of way, right to drive through, C.—Esp., a recital, delivery: fabella…

actutum.definition: āctūtum adv., immediately, forthwith: aperite ostium, T.: mortem actutum futuram puto: actutum in Italiā fore, L.

aculeatus.definition: aculeātus adj. aculeus, with a sting. — Hence, stinging, sharp: litterae.—Cunning, subtle: sophismata.

aculeus.definition: aculeus ī, m acus, a sting: apis.—Meton., a point, L.—Fig., a sting, spur, goad: severitatis vestrae: orationis meae: ad animos stimulandos, L.

acumen.definition: acūmen inis, n acuo. — Prop., a point: stili: lignum: sine acumine, O.: commissa in unum tereti acumine crura, i. e. united in a tapering tail, O. — Fig., of the mind, etc., acuteness, keenness, sharpness: ingeniorum:…

acuo.definition: acuō uī, ūtus, ere 2 AC-, to sharpen, whet, point, make sharp: stridor serrae, cum acuitur: ferrum in me, V.: sagittas cote cruentā, H. — Fig., of the tongue, to sharpen, exercise, practise: linguam causis, H. — Of th…

acus.definition: acus ūs, f 2 AC-, a needle: volnus acu punctum: pingere acu, to embroider, V.

acute.definition: acūtē adv. with comp. and sup. acutus, sharply; hence, of sound, shrilly, in a high key: sonare. —Fig., shrewdly, with discernment, pointedly: respondere: conlecta crimina: acutius tractare: acutissime scripta.

acutulus.definition: acūtulus adj. dim. acutus, rather keen: conclusiones.

acutus.definition: acūtus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of acuo, sharpened, pointed, sharp, cutting: sudes, Cs.: ferrum, H.: aures, pointed, H.: acuta leto Saxa (i. e. ad letum dandum), H.—Fig., to the senses, sharp, pungent, shrill: sonu…

ad.definition: ad praep. with acc. cf. Eng. at.—Of approach (opp. to ab, as in to ex). I. In space, to, toward: retorquet oculos ad urbem: una pars vergit ad septentriones, Cs.: tendens ad sidera palmas, V. —Fig.: ad alia vitia prop…

adactio.definition: adāctiō ōnis, f adigo, a compelling, exaction (once): iuris iurandi, L.

adaeque.definition: ad-aequē adv., in like manner, so also, L.

adaequo.definition: ad-aequō āvī, ātus, āre, to make equal, equalize, level with: cum virtute fortunam: cum familiarissimis eius adaequatus, regarded as his equal: molibus ferme (oppidi) moenibus adaequatis, on a level with, Cs.: tecta s…

adamanteus.definition: adamantēus adj. adamas, hard as steel, adamantine, not to be broken (poet.): nares, O.

adamantinus.definition: 'adamantinus adj., a)dama/ntinos, hard as steel, inflexible: clavis, H.: tunica, a coat of mail, H.: iuga, Pr.'

adamas.definition: adamās antis, m, a)da/mas, adamant, hardest iron, steel: solido adamante columnae, V.—Fig., of character: in pectore adamanta gerere, O.

adamo.definition: ad-amō āvī, ātus, āre, to fall in love with, conceive desire for, desire eagerly: cum signa pulcherrima vidisset, adamavit: agros, Cs.— Meton., to admire exceedingly, approve: patientiam: Platonem, N.

adaperio.definition: ad-aperiō eruī, ertus, īre, to throw open, open wide, lay open: cuniculum, L.: ianuam, O.—Fig., to open, expose: ad criminationem aures, Cu.—To disclose, reveal, expose: quae velanda erant, L.

adapertilis.definition: 'adapertilis e, adj. adaperio, that may be opened: latus tauri, O.'

adapertus.definition: 'adapertus adj. P. of adaperio, open, wide open: ora, O.'

adaquor.definition: ad-aquor —, ārī, dep., to obtain water, fetch water (once): adaquandi causā, Cs.

adaugeo.definition: ad-augeō auxī, auctus, ēre, to increase by adding, augment: ne tua duritia adaucta sit, T.: maleficia aliis nefariis: crimen, magnify.

adaugesco.definition: adaugēscō —, —, ere, inch. adaugeo, to grow, increase: stridor scopulorum.

adbibo.definition: ad-bibō bibī, —, ere, to take in by drinking: ubi adbibit plus paulo, has drunk a little too much, T.—Fig., to drink in, listen eagerly to: puro pectore verba, H.

addenseo.definition: ad - dēnseō —, —, ēre, to crowd together: extremi addensent acies, V.

addenso.definition: ad-dēnsō —, —, āre, in some edd. of V. for addenseo.

addico.definition: ad - dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to give assent.—In augural lang., to be propitious, favor: nisi aves addixissent, L.: in Termini fano, L.—In law: alicui aliquid or aliquem, to award, adjudge, sentence: bona alicui.—Esp.,…

addictio.definition: addictiō ōnis, f an award, adjudging (rare): bonorum.

addisco.definition: ad-discō didicī, —, ere, to learn in addition, gain knowledge of: cottidie aliquid: regimen carinae flectere, O.

additamentum.definition: additāmentum ī, n addo, an accession: inimicorum meorum, i. e. reinforcement.

addo.definition: ad-dō didī, ditus, ere do, to put to, place upon, lay on, join, attach: album in vestimentum, i. e. appear as a candidate, L.: turrim moenibus, O.: me adde fraternis sepulcris, lay me too in my brother's tomb, O.: nom…

addoceo.definition: ad - doceō —, —, ēre, to teach in addition (once): artes, i. e. new, H.

addubito.definition: ad-dubitō āvī, ātus, āre, to entertain a doubt, incline to doubt, hesitate, be uncertain: paulisper addubitavit, an, etc., was in doubt whether, etc., L.: illud addubitat, utrum, etc, leaves in doubt, N.: parumper, an…

adduco.definition: ad-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere (imper. adduce for adduc, T.— Perf. addūxtī for addūxistī, T.), to lead to, bring to, bring along (usu. of persons; cf. adfero, of things): quos Maecenas adduxerat umbras, brought along, H.: …

adducte.definition: adductē adv. adduco, strictly, severely; only comp: adductius regnari, Ta.

adductus.definition: 'adductus adj. P. of adduco, strict, severe: Nero, Ta.: servitium, Ta.'

adedo.definition: (ad-edō) ēdī, ēsus, ere, to eat away, gnaw at, consume: iecur, L.: favos, V.—Meton., of fire, to consume: flamma postibus haesit adesis, V.— Of water: lapides adesos, worn by water, H.— Fig.: adesa pecunia, used up: f…

ademptio.definition: adēmptiō ōnis, f adimo, a taking away, depriving: civitatis, of citizenship: bonorum, Ta.

adeo1.definition: ad-eō iī (rarely īvī), itus, īre, to go to, come to, come up to, approach, draw near: ad eum? T.: ad istum fundum: ad arbitrum, to submit a cause to a referee: in conventum: in ius, to go to law: ad praetorem in ius: …

adeo2.definition: ad-eō adv. I. To designate a limit, to this, thus far, so far, as far.— Of space, fig.: postremo adeo res rediit, finally it comes to this, T.—Of time, so long (as), so long (till): nusquam destitit ... orare usque ad…

adeps.definition: adeps ipis, comm, the soft fat of non-ruminating animals, fat.—Meton.: Cassi adipes, corpulence.

adeptio.definition: adeptiō ōnis, f adipiscor, an obtaining, attainment: boni; alicuius commodi.

adequito.definition: ad - equitō āvī, —, āre, to ride to, gallop to, ride up: ad nostros, Cs.: in primos ordines, Cu.: quo, L.: portis, L.: ab suis, L.

adesdum.definition: adesdum better ades dum (imper. of adsum with dum), come to me, stand by me (once), T.

adfabilis.definition: adfābilis (aff-) e, adj. ad-for, approachable, courteous, affable, kind, friendly: in sermone omnibus: nec dictu adfabilis ulli, V.

adfabilitas.definition: adfābilitās (aff-) ātis, f adfabilis, courtesy, affability: sermonis.

adfabre.definition: adfabrē (aff-) adv. ad + faber, cunningly, in a workmanlike manner: (deus) factus.

adfatim.definition: ad-fatim (aff-) adv. 2 FA-, satisfactorily, sufficiently, abundantly: satiata: parare commeatum, S.: vesci seminibus.—With gen part.: habetis adfatim lignorum, L.: pecuniae, L.

adfatus.definition: (adfātus or aff-) ūs, m ad-for, an accosting, speaking to; only abl., V.

adfectatio.definition: adfectātiō (aff-) ōnis, f adfecto, a claiming: Germanicae originis, Ta.

adfectio.definition: adfectiō (aff-) ōnis, f adficio, a relation, disposition: ad res reliquas.—Esp., a temporary state, perturbation: animi.—A frame, state, constitution: animi: corporis.—Fig., of the stars, position, aspect: astrorum: c…

adfecto.definition: adfectō (aff-) āvī, ātus, āre, freq. adficio, to strive after, strive to obtain, aspire to, pursue, aim at: imperium in Latinos, L.: honorem, S.: Gallias, Ta.: immortalitatem, lay claim to, Cu.—Esp., to cling to, cher…

adfectus1.definition: adfectus (aff-) adj. P. of adficio, furnished, supplied, endowed, provided, gifted: audaciā, T.: virtutibus. — Praegn., affected, impaired, weakened, infirm: animi, discouraged, L.: gravi morbo: ita adfectus, ut si ad…

adfectus2.definition: adfectus (aff-) ūs, m ad + 2 FAC-, a state, disposition, mood: animi: dubiis adfectibus errare, in vacillating moods, O.: adfectu tacito laetari, rapture, O.—A desire, fondness for: opes atque inopiam pari adfectu con…

adfero.definition: ad-ferō (aff-) attulī (adt-), adlātus (all-), adferre (aff-), to bring, fetch, carry, convey, take, deliver: magnam partem ad te, T.: scyphos ad praetorem: Curio pondus auri: nuntium ei: donum in Capitolium: litterae …

adficio.definition: adficiō (aff-) fēcī, fectus, ere ad + facio, to do to, treat, use, manage, handle: exercendum corpus et ita adficiendum, ut, etc.: quonam modo ille vos vivus adficeret, qui, etc., i. e. how would he treat you if alive…

adfigo.definition: ad-fīgō (aff-) fīxī, fīxus, ere, to fasten, attach, affix, annex: litteram ad caput: alqm cuspide ad terram, L.: Minervae talaria: Prometheus adfixus Caucaso: alqm terrae, L.: lecto te adfixit, confined, H.: flammam l…

adfingo.definition: ad-fingō (aff-) finxī, fictus, ere, to form as an addition, make besides, attach, affix, append: pars corporis sine necessitate adficta. — Fig., to add, contribute, bestow in addition: tantum (discipulo), ut, etc.— Es…

adfinis1.definition: ad-fīnis (aff-) e, adj. (abl. īnī, C.; once īne, T.), adjoining, bordering on: fundo: gens Mauris, L.—Fig., related by marriage: Hegio nobis, T.— Hence, subst.

adfinis2.definition: adfīnis is, m and f a connection by marriage: si me alienus adfinem volet, wants to marry into my family, T.: adfinem reppulisti. —Connected with, sharing, accessory to, implicated in: turpitudini: sceleri: illarum re…

adfinitas.definition: adfīnitās (aff-) ātis, f adfinis, relationship by marriage: inter nos, T.: in affinitatem alcuius pervenire, N.: adfinitatibus coniuncti, Cs.

adfirmate.definition: adfīrmātē (aff-) adv. adfirmo, with solemn assurance: promittere.

adfirmatio.definition: adfīrmātiō (aff-) ōnis, f adfirmo, an affirmation, asseveration, solemn assurance: religiosa: de reliquis civitatibus, Cs.: multa, Cu.

adfirmo.definition: ad-fīrmō (aff-) āvī, ātus, āre, to strengthen.— Fig., to confirm, encourage: Troianis spem, L.— Meton., to confirm, maintain, aver, positively assert, give solemn assurance of: nihil: rem pro certo, L.: se plus non da…

adfixus.definition: adfīxus adj. P. of adfigo, joined, attached: mihi esse adfixum, to keep close to me: in asperrimis saxulis: causa in animo, impressed.

adflatus.definition: adflātus (aff-) ūs, m ad-flo, a blowing on, breeze, blast, breath: ex terrā: vaporis, L: adflatu nocent, by the effluvia, O.: frondes adflatibus (apri) ardent, by his breath, O.—Fig., inspiration: divinus: furoris.

adflictatio.definition: adflīctātiō (aff-) ōnis, f adflicto, physical pain, torture.

adflicto.definition: adflīctō (aff-) āvī, ātus, āre, freq. adfligo, to break to pieces, destroy, shatter, damage, injure: qui Catuli monumentum adflixit: navīs tempestas adflictabat, Cs.: quod (naves) in vadis adflictarentur, were broken …

adflictor.definition: adflīctor (aff-) ōris, m adfligo, one who strikes down; fig., a subverter (once): dignitatis.

adflictus.definition: adflīctus (aff-) adj. with comp. P. of adfligo, cast down, miserable, unfortunate, overthrown, wretched, distressed: adflictum erexit: excitare adflictos: amicitia: fortunae reliquiae: adflictiore conditione: res suae…

adfligo.definition: ad-flīgō (aff-) īxī, īctus, ere, to dash at, strike upon, throw down, overthrow: statuam: monumentum: si quo adflictae casu conciderunt (alces), Cs.: ad quos (scopulos) adflictam navem videres.— Meton., to damage, inj…

adflo.definition: ad-flō (aff-) āvī, —, āre, to blow on, breathe upon: terga tantum adflante vento, L.: me ful minis ventis, blasted with, V.: qui (odores) adflarentur e floribus: taurorum adflabitur ore, i. e. scorched by the breath, …

adfluens.definition: adfluēns (aff-) entis, adj. with comp. P. of adfluo, flowing, abounding, abundant, rich, copious, affluent, numerous, plentiful: omnium rerum adfluentibus copiis: adfluentior amicitia: pauci opibus et copiis adfluente…

adfluenter.definition: '(adfluenter) adv. adfluens, lavishly, abundantly; only comp: adfluentius haurire: vivere, N.: adfluentius solito convivium inire, Ta.'

adfluentia.definition: 'adfluentia (aff-) ae, f adfluo, a flowing to; hence, fig., affluence, abundance, copiousness: rerum omnium: munditiem, non adfluentiam adfectabat, extravagance, N.'

adfluo.definition: adfluō (aff-) fluxī, fluxus, ere, to flow to, flow towards, flow by: amnis utrisque castris adfluens, L.—Fig., to glide quietly: nihil rumoris adfluxit, i. e. was heard.—To stream towards, in philos., of ideas: cum in…

adfor.definition: ad-for (aff-) ātus, ārī, dep., only praes ind. adfātur, adfāminī; imperf. adfābar (once); imper. adfāre; infin. adfā rī; part. adfātus.—In gen., to speak to, say to, address, accost: Pyrrham, O.: hos adfabar, V.: host…

adfulgeo.definition: (adfulgeō or aff-) ulsī, —, ēre (only perf. stem), to shine upon, beam, glitter, appear bright, be radiant: voltus tuus Adfulsit populo, H.: caeli ardentis species adfulserat, L. — Fig.: Hoc senatū s consulto facto, l…

adfundo.definition: ad-fundō (aff-) fūdī, fūsus, ere, to pour into, administer: alicui venenum, Ta.: Rhenum Oceano, Ta. — Pass, to fall down, prostrate oneself: Amplecti pedes adfusaque poscere vitam, O.: adfusae <*>acent tumulo, prostra…

adhaereo.definition: ad-haereō —, —, ēre, to cleave, adhere, stick to: vincto in corpore, cling to, O.: lateri quā pectus adhaeret, joins, O.: quibus (saxis) adhaerebant, L.: lentis adhaerens bracchiis, H.: manūs oneri adhaerentes, i. e. …

adhaeresco.definition: ad-haerēscō haesī, haesus, ere, inch. adhaereo, to cleave, stick, adhere: tragula ad turrim, Cs.: summusque in margine versus adhaesit, i. e. was added on the verge of the tablet, O.: adhaerescere ad columnam (Maeniam…

adhaesio.definition: adhaesiō ōnis, f an adhering, clinging (once).

adhibeo.definition: ad-hibeō uī, itus, ēre habeo, to hold toward, turn to, apply, add to: manūs medicas ad volnera, V.: ad panem adhibere, eat with: manū s genibus adhibet, i. e. clasps, O.—Fig., to furnish, produce, bring forward, apply…

adhinnio.definition: ad-hinniō īvī, —, īre, to neigh to, whinny to: equo, O.—Fig.: ad orationem, i. e. expressed delight.

adhortatio.definition: adhortātiō ōnis, f adhortor, an encouragement, exhortation: nostra: clamore conprobata, L.: invicem, L.: mutua, Cu.—Plur., L.

adhortator.definition: adhortātor ōris, m adhortor, one who encourages: operis, to the work, L.

adhortor.definition: ad-hortor ātus, ārī, to encourage, exhort, stimulate, rouse, urge: milites: me ad Rabirium defendendum: Boios de re frumentariā, Cs.: adulescentes, ut turbulenti velint esse: adhortor, properent, T.: in bellum, Ta.

adhuc.definition: ad - hūc adv. of time, until now, heretofore, hitherto, as yet: sicut adhuc fecerunt, speculabuntur: unde est adhuc bellum tractum, nisi, etc., all this time: adhuc ignota precatur flumina, hitherto, V.: qui me passus…

adiaceo.definition: ad-iaceō cuī, —, ēre, to lie at, lie near, adjoin, border upon, touch, bound: Tuscus ager Romano adiacet, L.: adiacet undis moles, O.: gentes, quae mare illud adiacent, N.: Etruriam, L.: (regio) ad Aduatucos, Cs.: adi…

adicio.definition: adiciō (pronounced adiiciō), iēcī, iectus, ere ad + iacio, to throw to, cast to, fling at, put, put to, set near: hordei numero ad summam tritici adiecto: Adiectoque cavae supplentur sanguine venae, O.: telum ex locis…

adiectio.definition: adiectiō ōnis, f adicio, an annexation, addition: populi Albani, L.: inliberali adiectione, i. e. by grudgingly adding (to his offer), L.

adigo.definition: adigō ēgī, āctus, ere ad + ago, to drive, urge, bring by force, take (to a place): pecore ex longinquioribus vicis adacto, Cs.— Of persons: te adiget horsum insomnia, T.: aliquem fulmine ad umbras, V.: Italiam vos? V.…

adimo.definition: adimō ēmī, ēmptus, ere ad + emo, to take away, take from, deprive of: Multa ferunt anni commoda, Multa recedentes adimunt, H.: metum, T.: adimere aegritudinem hominibus, to free men from sorrow, T.: qui das adimisque …

adipatus.definition: adipātus adj. adeps, fat, greasy. — Plur. neut. as subst, pastry prepared with fat: livida, Iu.—Of discourse, coarse, gross: dictio.

adipiscor.definition: adipīscor adeptus, ī, dep. ad + apiscor, to come up with, arrive at, reach, overtake: Romani adepti fessos, L.—Fig., to attain, get, obtain, acquire, reach: senectutem: hanc victoriam, Cs.: tuam amicitiam, N.: ius nos…

aditus2.definition: aditus ūs, m 1 adeo, a going to, drawing near, approach, access: urbī s uno aditu atque adventu captas: temptare aditūs, seek to approach, V.: viri mollīs aditūs novisse, how to approach gently, V.—A privilege of admi…

adiudico.definition: ad-iūdicō āvī, ātus, āre, to make a judicial award, grant, award, adjudge: regnum Ptolemaeo: alcui magistratum, Cs.: alqd Italis adiudicat armis, adds to the Roman Empire (poet. of Augustus), H.: causam alcui, to deci…

adiumentum.definition: adiūmentum ī, n for adiuvamentum; adiuvo, a means of helping, help, aid, support, assistance: adiumenta et subsidia consulatūs: adiumenta rerum gerundarum, natural advantages: ignaviae, S.: nihil adiumenti ad pulchrit…

adiunctio.definition: adiūnctiō ōnis, f adiungo, a joining, union, conjunction: homini ad hominem naturae. — In rhet., the connection of a predicate with several subjects, C.—An addition to: virtutis.

adiunctor.definition: adiūnctor ōris, m adiungo, he who adds: Galliae ulterioris, i. e. Pompey.

adiunctus.definition: adiūnctus adj. with comp. P. of adiungo, closely connected, joined, united: quae huius causae adiunctiora sunt: huic fundo praedia.—As subst n., a characteristic, adjunct, essential attribute: in adiunctis morabimur, …

adiungo.definition: adiungō ūnxī, ūnctus, ere, to fasten on, join to, harness: plostello mures, H.: ulmis vites, V.: remos lateribus, Ta. — Fig., to join, attach: ad imperium populi R. Ciliciam: (urbes) consilio ad amicitiam, won over by…

adiuro.definition: ad-iūrō āvī, —, āre, to swear to in addition, attest besides, add to an oath: praeter commune ius iurandum haec, L.—To add an oath, swear to, confirm by oath: omnia: adiuras id te non esse facturum: in quae adactus es…

adiuto.definition: adiūtō āvī, —, āre, freq. adiuvo, to help zealously, serve, aid, assist (old or late): senem, T.: funus, to aid in, T.: eis (pueris) onera adiuta, help them carry, T.: id adiuta me, T.

adiutor.definition: adiūtor ōris, m adiuvo, a helper, assistant, confederate: alcuius honoris: cuius honori semper adiutor fuerit, Cs.: his adiutoribus in re gerendā uti: ad res gerendas, L.: quīs adiutoribus, and with their aid, S.— Esp…

adiutrix.definition: adiūtrīx īcis, f adiutor, she that helps, a female assistant: matres filiis adiutrices solent esse, T.: scelerum.

adiuvo.definition: ad-iuvō iūvī (adiuerō, old for adiūverō), iū tus, āre, to help, assist, aid, support, further, sustain: fortīs fortuna adiuvat, T.: maerorem orationis meae lacrimis suis: suā sponte eos, N.: pennis adiutus amoris, O.:…

adlabor.definition: ad-lābor (all-) apsus sum, ī, dep., to glide towards, flow, glide, slide: viro adlapsa sagitta, V.: oris, arrive at, V.: aurīs, reach, V.: mare crescenti adlabitur aestu, rolls up as the tide rises, V.: extrinsecus: e…

adlaboro.definition: ad-labōrō (all-) —, —, āre, to labor, toil: ore adlaborandum est tibi, ut, etc., H. — With dat, to add to by labor: myrto nihil adlabores, H.

adlacrimo.definition: ad-lacrimō (all-) —, —, āre, to shed tears thereat, weep (once): Iuno adlacrimans, V.

adlapsus.definition: adlapsus (all-) ūs, m adlabor, a gliding up to, stealthy approach: plur.: serpentium, H.

adlatro.definition: ad-lātrō (all-) —, āre, to bark at. — Fig., to rail at, revile: magnitudinem Africani, L.

adlecto.definition: adlectō (all-) —, āre, freq. adlicio, to allure, entice: ad (agrum) fruendum: vanitatem, court.

adlegatio.definition: adlēgātiō (all-) ōnis, f 1 adlego, a sending, despatching: ad istum.

adlego1.definition: ad-lēgō (all-) āvī, ātus, āre, to send on business, despatch, commission, depute, charge: te ad illos: homines nobilī s: a me adlegatus senex, instigated, T.

adlego2.definition: ad - legō (all-) ēgī, ēctus, ere, to select, choose, elect: augures de plebe, L.

adlevamentum.definition: adlevāmentum (all-) ī, n adlevo, a mitigation, relief: sine ullo adlevamento.

adlevatio.definition: adlevātiō (all-) ōnis, f adlevo, an alleviation: doloris diuturnitatem adlevatio consoletur.

adlevo.definition: ad-levō (all-) āvī, ātus, āre, to lift up, raise, set up: oculos, Cu.: (laqueis) adlevati (milites), S.: cubito artūs, O. — Fig., to lighten, alleviate, comfort, console: aerumnam dictis: adlevatum corpus tuum, recove…

adlicio.definition: ad-liciō (all-) lexī, lectus, ere ad + lacio, to allure, entice, attract, persuade, influence: multorum opes ad misericordiam: somnos, O.: hominum studia: ad amicitiam (similitudo).—Fig. of the magnet: ferrum ad se, a…

adlido.definition: ad-līdō (all-) līsī, līsus, ere ad + laedo, to strike upon, dash against: ad scopulos, Cs.—Fig., to ruin.

adligo.definition: ad-ligō (all-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bind to, tie to: reliquos ad palum.—Esp., to bind up, bandage: volnus, L.—To fetter, shackle: adligari se patitur, Ta.—To hold fast: adligat ancora (navī s), V.— Fig., to hinder, deta…

adlino.definition: ad-linō (all-) —, —, ere, to besmear: incomptis (versibus) signum, i. e. to erase, H. — Fig., to attach, impart: sordes sententiis.

adlocutio.definition: adlocūtiō (all-) ōnis, f adloquor, a consoling, comforting: Quā solatus es adlocutione? Ct.

adloquium.definition: adloquium (all-) ī, n adloquor, an exhortation, encouragement: benignum, L.—Plur, solaces: aegrimoniae, H.

adloquor.definition: ad-loquor (all-) cūtus, ī, dep., to speak to, address, salute, greet: hominem, T.: hunc claviger adloquitur, O.: patriam maestā voce, Ct.— Esp., to exhort, rouse: milites, L.

adludo.definition: ad-lūdō (all-) ūsī, —, ere, to play, sport, joke, jest, do sportively: ad id, T.: varie et copiose: adludit (Ino Tauro), O.: nec plura adludens, dwelling longer on the jest, V.: qui occupato adluserit, jested with him…

adluo.definition: ad-luō (all-) uī, —, ere, to flow near to, wash against, bathe: non adluuntur a mari moenia: urbs mari adluitur, L.: mare, quod adluit (Italiam) infra, V.—Fig., to beset: (Massilia) barbariae fluctibus adluitur.

adluvies.definition: adluviēs (all-) —, abl. ē, f 3 LV-, an inundation, L. dub.

adluvio.definition: adluviō (all-) ōnis, f 3 LV-, an inundation.

admaturo.definition: ad-mātūrō —, —, āre, to mature (once): seditionem, Cs.

admetior.definition: ad-mētior mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure out: tibi frumentum.

adminiculo.definition: adminiculō āre adminiculum, to prop: vitem (once).

adminiculum.definition: adminiculum ī, n MA-, MAN-.—In vineyards, a stake, prop: vites adminicula adprehendunt: adminiculorum ordines.—In gen., a support, stay: ipsis adminiculis prolapsis, the limbs, L.: corporis, Cu. — Fig., help, aid: id …

administer.definition: ad - minister trī, m one who is at hand to help, an assistant, minister, helper: administris ad ea sacrificia Druidibus utuntur, Cs.: consiliorum, S. — Esp., a tool, instrument, pandar: Naevi: istius cupiditatum.—An e…

administra.definition: ad-ministra ae, f administer, a female assistant, handmaid.—Fig.: artes administrae virtutis.

administratio.definition: administrātiō ōnis, f administro, aid, help, co-operation: hominum.—Direction, management, administration: mundi: tormentorum, Cs.: portūs, Cs.

administrator.definition: administrātor ōris, m administro, a manager, conductor: belli gerendi.

administro.definition: ad-ministrō āvī, ātus, āre, to manage, control, guide, superintend, execute, regulate, rule, direct: provinciam: rem p., C., L.: bellum, Cs.: per homines honestissimos leges: legationes per Dionem, N.: alqd privato co…

admirabilis.definition: admīrābilis e, adj. with comp. admiror, admirable, wonderful: clementia: in dicendo homines. —Esp., strange, like paradox.

admirabilitas.definition: admīrābilitās ātis, f admirabilis, admirableness: magna.

admirabiliter.definition: admīrābiliter adv. admirabilis, wonderfully, admirably: laudari.—Paradoxically: dicere.

admirandus.definition: admīrandus adj. P. of admiror, to be wondered at, admirable, wonderful: homo: admirandum in modum, N.: spectacula, V.

admiratio.definition: admīrātiō ōnis, f admiror, admiration, wonder: admiratione adfici: admirationis plus habere quam gloriae. — Plur, expressions of admiration, applause: admirationes in oratoribus efficere: copiose sapienterque dicentis…

admirator.definition: admīrātor ōris, m admiror, an admirer: Simonidis, Ph.

admiror.definition: ad-mīror ātus, ārī, dep., to regard with wonder, admire: eorum ingenia, T.: illum, V.: eum in his, N.—To regard with wonder, wonder at, be astonished: stultitiam, N.: quicquam, T.: in uno homine tantam esse dissimilit…

admisceo.definition: ad - misceō scuī, xtus (mīstus), ēre, to add so as to form a mixture, mix with, admix: admixto calore: ille (aër) multo calore admixtus est: aquae calorem. — Fig., to mingle, mix in with: huic generi orationis illud a…

admissarius.definition: admissārius ī, m admitto, a stallion.

admissum.definition: ad-missum ī, n admitto, a voluntary fault, trespass, crime: nullo admisso: tale, L.: gentis dolosae, O.: Poppaeae, Ta.

admitto.definition: ad-mittō mīsī, missus, ere (admittier, old for admitti, V.), to send to, let go, let loose, let come, admit, give access: te ad meas capsas admisero: domum ad se filium, N.: Iovis arcanis Minos admissus, H. — Esp., to…

admixtio.definition: admīxtiō ōnis, f admisceo, a mingling.— Fig., association, union.

admodum.definition: ad-modum adv.; prop., to the proper limit, to full measure; hence, with numerals, full, quite, at least, no less than: noctu turres admodum CXX excitantur, full, Cs.: equites, mille admodum, a round thousand, Cu.; no …

admolior.definition: ad-mōlior ītus, īrī, dep., to bring hither: rupes, Cu.

admoneo.definition: ad-moneō nuī, nitus, ēre, to bring to mind, remind, suggest, put in mind of: te: (me) equorum, O.: alqm foederis, L.: admonitus re ipsā recordor quantum, etc.: deorum ira admonuit, aroused him, L.: de quo (proelio) vo…

admonitio.definition: admonitiō ōnis, f admoneo, a suggestion, reminding: vis admonitionis. — An exhortation, admonition: in consilio dando.

admonitor.definition: admonitor ōris, m admoneo, an admonisher, exhorter: admonitore egere: operum, to labor, O.

admonitum.definition: admonitum ī, n admoneo, a reminding, warning, C., O.

admonitus.definition: (admonitus) —, m admoneo, a reminding, suggestion, request.— Only abl sing.: admonitu Allobrogum: tuo. — Reproof: acrior admonitu est, more violent for the reproof, O.

admorsus.definition: 'ad-morsus P. ad + mordeo, bitten, gnawed: stirps, V.: bracchia colubris, Pr.'

admotio.definition: admōtiō ōnis, f admoveo, an application: digitorum, to the chords.

admoveo.definition: ad - moveō mōvī (admōrunt, V.), mōtus, ēre, to move to, move towards, bring up, bring near, carry, conduct, drive: fasciculum (florum) ad narīs: ora ad ora, O.: exercitum ad urbem, L.: scalis admotis; applied, Cs.: la…

admugio.definition: ad-mūgiō —, —, īre, to low to, bellow to: tauro, O.

admurmuratio.definition: admurmurātiō ōnis, f admurmuro, a murmuring, murmur: vestra: senatūs frequentis: grata contionis.

admurmuro.definition: ad-murmurō āvī, ātus, āre, to murmur, murmur at: valde: cum esset admurmuratum: admurmurante Senatu.

adnato.definition: ad-natō —, —, āre, to swim up: certatim, Ph.

adnecto.definition: ad-nectō (ann-) nexuī, nexus, ere, to tie to, bind to, fasten on, attach, annex: scapha adnexa: ratis adnexa vinculis, L.: rebus praesentibus futuras: magnis domibus adnexa, akin, Ta.—To subjoin, add, Ta.

adnexus.definition: (adnexus or ann-) —, m ad-necto, a connection, association: adnexu gentium florere, Ta.

adnitor.definition: ad-nītor (ann-) nīxus or nīsus, dep., to lean against, lean upon: ad aliquod tamquam adminiculum: adnixi hastis, V. — Fig., to take pains, make an effort, exert oneself, strive: acrius ut, etc., S.: pro se quisque, ut…

adno.definition: ad-nō (ann-) āvī, —, āre, to swim to, swim up to: oris, V.: navibus, L.: navīs, Cs.: adnabunt thynni, H.—Fig.: ad urbem, approach.—To swim beside: equis, Ta.

adnoto.definition: ad-notō avī, —, āre, to observe, remark: Adnotabant periti, etc., Ta.: adnotatus est (with infin.), Ta.

adnumero.definition: ad-numerō (ann-) āvī, ātus, āre, to add, join, count among: his libris adnumerandi sunt sex.— To count out, pay down, pay: argentum, T.: alqd Apronio.—Fig., to count out: non adnumerare ea (verba) lectori, sed appende…

adnuntio.definition: ad - nūntiō (ann-) —, —, āre, to announce, make known. — Pass. with acc. and inf., Cu.

adnuo.definition: ad-nuō (ann-) uī (adnuērunt, trisyl., H.), —, ere, to nod to, make a sign: sibi: adnuentibus ac vocantibus suis, L.—To signal, hint: an destringeret gladium, i. e. to ask by a sign, Ta.: ut considerem, Cu.— To give as…

adoleo.definition: adoleō oluī, —, ēre 2 OD-, OL-, to turn to vapor; hence, to burn in sacrifice: Verbenasque, V.: Iunoni iussos honores, the prescribed burntofferings, V.: altaria taedis, to fire up, V.: flammis Penatīs, to fill with s…

adolesco1.definition: ad-olēscō (adul-) olēvī, ultus, ere, to grow up, come to maturity, ripen: sensim: simul atque adoleverit aetas, as soon as his age is mature, H.— Fig., to grow, mature, become great: ingenium brevi adolevit, S.: postq…

adolesco2.definition: adolēscō —, —, ere, inch. adoleo, to burn, blaze up, flame: adolescunt ignibus arae, V.

adoperio.definition: ad-operiō eruī, ertus, īre, >to cover, cover over: capite adoperto, L.: Purpureo adopertus amictu, V.: lumina somno, buried, O.

adoptatio.definition: adoptātiō ōnis, f adopto, an adopting, adoption: filiorum: adoptatione in regnum pervenisse, S.

adoptio.definition: ādoptiō ōnis, f adopto, a taking as a child, adoption: ius adoptionis: dare filium in adoptionem, L.

adoptivus.definition: adoptīvus adj. adopto, of adoption: sacra, obtained by adoption: nobilitas, O. — Of fruits, grafted, O.

adopto.definition: ad-optō āvī, ātus, āre, to take by choice, select, choose, adopt: alqm sibi defensorem sui iuris: eum sibi patronum. —Esp., to take into a family, adopt as a child: eum adoptavit heredemque fecit, N.: alqm in regnum, …

ador.definition: ador (nom. and acc.), n a grain, spelt, H.

adorea.definition: adōrea (not -ria), ae, f adoreus, a prize of valor (anciently a gift of grain). — Hence, praise, glory: alma, H.

adoreus.definition: adōreus adj. ador, of spelt: liba, V.

adorior.definition: ad-orior ortus, īrī, dep., to approach as an enemy, fall upon, assail, assault, attack: a tergo Milonem: hominem tumultuosissime: tribunum gladiis: impeditos, Cs.: urbem vi, L.: oppugnatio eos atrocior adorta est, L. …

adorno.definition: ad-ōrnō āvī, ātus, āre, to provide, furnish, fit out, equip, make ready: forum ornatu: opulentiā armorum bellum, L.: navī s, Cs.: petitionem consulatūs, to prepare: testium copiam: maria classibus: haec adornant ut la…

adoro.definition: ad-ōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to call upon, entreat, supplicate, implore: prece numen, V.: adorati di, ut bene eveniret, L.: maneat, adoro, Pr.: pacem deum, i. e. the favor of the gods, L.—To reverence, honor, worship: Phoeb…

adquiesco.definition: ad-quiēscō (acqu-) ēvī, ere, to become quiet, come to rest, rest, repose: trīs horas: somno, Cu.: anno septuagesimo, to die, N. — Fig., to become quiet, be at rest, have peace: civitas adquiescens: rem familiarem adqu…

adquiro.definition: adquīrō (acqu-) quīsīvī, quīsītus, ere ad + quaero, to get in addition, obtain besides, accumulate: nihil: novos amicos, S.: armis opes, L.: pauca (verba), i. e. add (to the language), H.: de possessione detrahere, ad…

adrado.definition: ad-rādō —, sus, ere, to scrape, cut short, shave: conspexit Adrasum quendam, close shaved, H.

adrectus.definition: adrēctus (arr-) adj. with comp. P. of adrigo, upright, erect, standing: constitit in digitos adrectus, V.: squamae, V.: Tollit se adrectum (equus), rears, V. — Meton., steep, precipitous: pleraque Alpium adrectiora, L…

adrepo.definition: ad-rēpō (arr-) rēpsī, —, ere, to creep to, steal up: ad istius amicitiam, insinuate himself: in spem, ut, etc., H.

adrideo.definition: ad-rīdeō (arr-) rīsī, rīsus, ēre, to laugh, smile at, laugh with, smile upon: alqd: cum dixisset ... arrisissetque adulescens: cum risi, adrides, O.: omnibus, T.: ut ridentibus adrident, on those who smile, H.—To be p…

adrigo.definition: ad-rigō (arr-) ēxī, ēctus, ere ad + rego, to set up, raise, erect: comas, V.: adrectis auribus (of horses), O.—Fig., to rouse, encourage, animate, excite: eos oratione, S.: spes adrectae iuvenum, V.: adrectae stimulis…

adripio.definition: ad-ripiō (arr-) ipuī, eptus, ere ad + rapio, to snatch, catch hurriedly, grasp, seize: telum: arcūs, O.: manum, H.—To seize, lay hold of: alqm medium, T.: quem adripuit, has buttonholed, H.: alqm comā, O.: adreptus de…

adrisio.definition: adrīsiō (arr-) ōnis, f adrideo, a smile of approval, Her.

adrodo.definition: ad-rōdō (arr-) sī, sus, ere, to nibble at, gnaw: mures coronam adrosere, L.: rem p.

adrogans.definition: adrogāns (arr-) antis, adj. (P. of adrogo), assuming, arrogant, haughty: si essent adrogantes: Chloe, H.: in praeripiendo populi beneficio, Cs.— With dat., minoribus, Ta.

adroganter.definition: 'adroganter (arr-) adv. with comp. adrogans, presumptuously, arrogantly, haughtily: scribere: facere, Cs.: consulere, Ta.: nihil dicam adrogantius.'

adrogantia.definition: adrogantia (arr-) ae, f adrogans, assumption, presumption, arrogance: sine adrogantiā gravis: ingeni.—Pride, haughtiness: eius: in conloquio, Cs.: in adrogantiam compositus, i. e. with haughty indifference, Ta.

adrogo.definition: ad-rogō (arr-) āvī, ātus, āre, to add, associate with. consuli dictatorem, L. — To appropriate, claim. sibi sapientiam: quantum mihi adrogo: sibi cenarum artem, H.: alqd ex alienā virtute sibi, S.— Poet.: alicui aliqu…

adsecla.definition: 'adsecla (ass-) ae, m for adsecula, a follower, attendant: praetoris, N.'

adsectatio.definition: adsectātiō (ass-) ōnis, f adsector, a waiting on, attendance: in petitionibus, personal solicitation.

adsectator.definition: adsectātor (ass-) ōris, m adsector, a client, follower: vetus.

adsector.definition: ad-sector (ass-) ātus, ārī, dep., to wait upon, follow; of clients, C.; of a bore, H.

adsecula.definition: 'adsecula (ass-) ae, m adsequor, a follower, sycophant: alcuius: humilis, Iu.'

adsensio.definition: adsēnsiō (ass-) ōnis, f adsentior, an assent, agreement, approval: popularis; plur: ordinis.—An acceptance as real, C.

adsensor.definition: adsēnsor (ass-) ōris, m one who agrees.

adsensus2.definition: adsēnsus (ass-) ūs, m adsentio, an agreement, assent, approval, approbation: omnium adsensu iudicare: partīs adsensibus implent, fulfil their duty by assent, O.—An acceptance as real, C.—Poet., an echo: nemorum, V.

adsentatio.definition: adsentātiō (ass-) ōnis, f adsentor, flattery, adulation: parasitorum: erga principem, Ta. —Plur., C., L.

adsentatiuncula.definition: adsentātiuncula (ass-) ae, f dim. adsentatio, a bit of flattery.

adsentator.definition: adsentātor (ass-) ōris, m adsentor, a flatterer, fawner: peniciosus: mulierum: regii, L.

adsentio.definition: ad-sentiō (ass-) sēnsī, sēnsus, īre, to agree with, assent, approve: Adsensere omnes, V.: eius voluntatibus: de aliis rebus, L.: multa ... adsensa, acknowledged as real: si tibi non sit adsensum.

adsentior.definition: ad - sentior (ass-) sēnsus, īrī, dep., to give assent, approve, agree with: omnes adsensi sunt, L.: clamori vestro: Sulpicio: illud: cetera Crasso: adsentior tibi, ut, etc.

adsentor.definition: adsentor (ass-) ātus, ārī, freq. adsentior, to assent constantly, flatter, fawn: id adsentandi (sc. causā) facere, T.: (adulator) adversando adsentetur: huic, T.: qui ipse sibi adsentetur: Omnia, in everything, T.: ni…

adsequor.definition: ad - sequor (ass-) secūtus, ī, dep., to follow up, overtake, come up with: adsequere, retine, T.: me.—Fig., to gain, reach, attain: honoris gradūs: merita: alqd scelere.—To effect, accomplish: alqd verbo: nihil, nisi …

adsero1.definition: ad - serō (ass-) —, situs, ere, to plant at, set near: pō pulus adsita Limitibus, H.: adsitae arbores, Ct.

adsero2.definition: ad-serō (ass-) seruī, sertus, ere, to claim, lay claim to, appropriate (poet.): laudes, O.: me caelo, i. e. as of heavenly origin, O.: Iovem sibi patrem, Cu.: virginem in servitutem, as his slave, L.: liberali illam c…

adsertor.definition: adsertor ōris, m 2 adsero, one who claims (as master): puellae, L.— A defender, advocate, O.

adservio.definition: ad - serviō (ass-) —, —, īre, to help, assist, strengthen (once): contentioni vocis.

adservo.definition: ad-servō (ass-) āvī, ātus, āre, to watch over, keep, preserve, guard: tabulae neglegentius adservatae: navīs: portas, Cs.: cura adservandum vinctum, have him kept under close guard, T.: ius: Vitrubium in carcerem adse…

adsessio.definition: adsessiō (ass-) ōnis, f adsideo, a sitting near.

adsessor.definition: adsessor (ass-) ōris, m adsideo, an assistant, aid.

adsessus.definition: adsessus (ass-) ūs, m adsideo, a sitting by: Turpior adsessu meo, from sitting by me, Pr.

adseveranter.definition: adsevēranter (ass-) adv. with comp. adsevero, earnestly, emphatically: loqui.

adseveratio.definition: adsevērātiō (ass-) ōnis, f adsevero, a vehement assertion, protestation: omni adseveratione adfirmo, most solemnly: magnā , Ta.

adsevero.definition: adsevērō (ass-) āvī, ātus, āre ad + severus, to affirm, insist on, maintain, assert, aver: se ab Oppianico destitutum: ullā de re: utrum adseveratur in hoc? Is this seriously maintained?—To show, prove: originem, Ta.

adsideo.definition: adsideō (ass-) ēdī, —, ēre ad + sedeo, to sit by, sit near: ibi, L.: nobis: huic: pullis (avis), H.: valetudini, attend, Ta.: habes qui Adsideat, H.: insano, i. e. is to be classed with, H.: in carcere. — To sit with …

adsido.definition: ad-sīdō (ass-) ēdī, —, ere, to take a seat, sit down, resume one's seat: adsidamus, si videtur: peroravit, adsedit, surrexi ego: Adherbalem, took a seat beside, S.

adsidue.definition: adsiduē (ass-) adv. with sup. adsiduus, continually, constantly, uninterruptedly: ubi sum adsidue, T.: canere: venire, V.: voces audire: adsiduissime mecum fuit.

adsiduitas.definition: adsiduitās (ass-) ātis, f adsiduus, constant attendance: medici: adsiduitatem tibi praebuisse: valuit adsiduitate, had influence by: alicuius in rem p., unremitting service: adsiduitate perficere ut, etc., by persiste…

adsiduus.definition: adsiduus (ass-) adj. ad + SED-, SID-, attending, continually present, busied: filius in praediis, occupied: agricolae, diligent: dominus, attentive to his business: in oculis hominum, habitually, L.: hostis, persisten…

adsignatio.definition: adsīgnātiō (ass-) ōnis, f adsigno, an assigning, allotting: agrorum: novae adsignationes.

adsigno.definition: ad-sīgnō (ass-) āvī, ātus, āre, to mark out, allot, assign, award: ad agrum adsignandum, L.: agrum militibus. — To allot, assign, appropriate: apparitores: equiti alqd, L.—To commit, intrust: quibus deportanda Romam I…

adsilio.definition: adsiliō (ass-) —, īre ad + salio, to leap at, spring upon: moenibus, O: tactus Adsilientis aquae, dashing up, O.—To pass suddenly: ad genus illud orationis.—To assault: viam, Ta.

adsimilis.definition: 'ad - similis (ass-) e, adj., like, similar: sui, O.: spongiis: fratribus, O.'

adsimulatio.definition: adsimulātiō ōnis, f a feigned assent, Her.

adsimulatus.definition: adsimulātus (ass-) adj. P. of adsimulo, feigned, pretended, fictitious: virtus: consuetudo, N.

adsimulo.definition: ad - simulō (ass-, -similō) āvī, ātus, ā re, to make like, liken, compare: convivia freto, O.: formam bipenni, Ta.: in humani oris speciem, Ta.— To copy, imitate: litterae lituraeque adsimulatae, exactly copied: iubas…

adsisto.definition: ad - sistō (ass-) astitī or adstitī, —, ere, to stand by, take a stand near, attend: accede, adsiste: in conspectu patris, i. e. appear, Cs.: ad forīs: divinis, H.: lecto, O.: ad epulas regis, serve.—To station onesel…

adsoleo.definition: ad-soleō (ass-) —, —, ēre (only 3d person), to be accustomed, be wont, be usual: quae adsolent signa esse ad salutem, T.: praebere vestigia sui, L.: ludos, tantā pecuniā, quantā adsoleret, faciendos, L.: ut adsolet, a…

adsono.definition: ad-sonō (ass-) —, —, āre, to resound, respond: plangentibus Echo, O.

adsuefacio.definition: adsuēfaciō (assuē-) fēcī, factus, ere adsuetus + facio, to accustom, habituate, inure: quorum sermone adsuefacti qui erunt: scelerum exercitatione: a pueris disciplinā, Cs.: pedites operi, L.: ad supplicium plebem, L.…

adsuesco.definition: ad-suēscō (assuē-) ēvī, ētus, ere, to accustom, habituate: pluribus mentem, H.: animis bella, make familiar, V.: caritas, cui adsuescitur, one becomes accustomed, L.—P. pass., habituated, accustomed: mensae erili, V.:…

adsuetudo.definition: adsuētūdō (assuē-) inis, f adsuetus, custom, habit: longa, O.: mali, L.: voluptatum, Ta.

adsuetus.definition: adsuētus (assuē-) adj. P. of adsuesco, accustomed, customary, familiar: oculis regio, L.: onus, O.: antra, O.: Longius adsueto videre, further than usual, O.; see adsuesco.

adsulto.definition: adsultō (ass-) āvī, ātus, āre, freq. adsilio, to leap at, attack, assault: latera, Ta.: tergis, Ta.

adsultus.definition: adsultus (ass-) ūs, m ad + 2 SAL-, an attack, assault.—Only abl plur.: variis adsultibus, V.: adsultibus uti, Ta.

adsum.definition: ad-sum (assum) adfuī (aff-), adesse (adsiet for adsit, T.; adfore for adfutūrum esse), to be at, be present, be at hand: quia ades praesens, T.: vos, qui adsunt: coram, V.: ad portam: ante oculos, V.: portis, V.: duci…

adsumo.definition: ad-sūmō (ass-) sūmpsī, sūmptus, ere, to take to oneself, receive: socios, L.: dignos, H.: umeris alas, O.: eos in societatem, L.: sacra Cereris de Graeciā: socius adsumitur Scaurus, S.: voluptas adsumenda est: equus p…

adsumptio.definition: adsūmptiō (ass-) ōnis, f adsumo, acceptance, adoption.— In logic, the minor premise.

adsumptivus.definition: adsūmptīvus (ass-) adj. adsumo. — In rhet., extraneous, extrinsic.

adsuo.definition: ad - suō (ass-) —, —, ere, to sew on, patch: inceptis ... Adsuitur pannus, H.

adsurgo.definition: ad - surgō (ass-) surrēxī, surrēctus, ere, to rise up, rise, stand up: adsurgite: querellis Haud iustis, V.: arbore fluctum Verberat adsurgens, rising to the oars, V.: adsurgentis dextrā Aeneae, towering, V.: quantus …

adulatio.definition: adūlātiō ōnis, f adulor, a fawning: canum. —Flattery, cringing courtesy: in amicitiis pestis ... adulatio: potentium, Cs.: in Augustum, Ta.

adulator.definition: adūlātor ōris, m a sycophant, Her.

adulescens.definition: adulēscēns (not adol-), ntis P. of adolesco, adj. with comp, growing, near maturity, young, youthful: admodum: adulescentior Academia, younger: homines, Cs.: filia. — As subst, m. and f a youth, young man or woman (be…

adulescentia.definition: adulēscentia (not adol-), ae, f adulescens, youth: mea: ineunte adulescentiā.—Youth, young men: laetatur.

adulescentula.definition: adulēscentula ae, f dim. adulescens, a young maiden, little girl, T.

adulescentulus.definition: adulēscentulus ī, m dim. adulescens, a very young man: ab adulescentulo, from boyhood, S.—Plur: stulti.

adulo.definition: adūlō —, —, āre, to fawn upon: sanguinem, to wipe off fawningly, Acc. ap. C.

adulor.definition: adūlor ātus, ārī, dep., to fawn: ferarum agmen adulantum, O.—To fawn upon, flatter, cringe: omnīs: aperte adulantem videre, to detect an open flatterer: plebi, L.

adulter.definition: adulter tera, adj. ad + 2 AL-, adulterous, unchaste: coniunx, O.: crines, seductive, H. — As subst, m. and f an adulterer, adulteress: sororis, adulterous seducer of: Lacaena, i. e. Helen, H.— A paramour, seducer, H.

adulterinus.definition: adulterīnus adj. adulter, false, forged, counterfeit: nummus: signa, a false seal.

adulterium.definition: adulterium ī, n adulter, adultery, C., V., O.

adultero.definition: adulterō āvī, ātus, āre, to commit adultery, C. —Trans, to mingle: adulteretur et columba miluo, H. — To falsify, corrupt: ius civile pecuniā, for a bribe: iudicium veri.

adultus.definition: 'adultus adj. 1 adolesco, grown up, mature, adult, ripe: virgo: crinis, Ct.: fetus (of bees), V.: vitium propago, mature, H.: aetas: rei p. pestis, inveterate: res nondum adultae, L.'

adumbratio.definition: adumbrātiō ōnis, f adumbro, a sketch, outline.

adumbratus.definition: adumbrātus adj. P. of adumbro, sketched, shadowed, in outline: dii: imago gloriae.—Apparent, feigned, unreal: comitia: Pippae vir, pretended husband: indicium, fictitious information.

adumbro.definition: adumbrō āvī, ātus, āre ad + umbra, to sketch in shadow, outline, represent vaguely: res expressa, non adumbrata.—To imitate, copy, Cu.

aduncitas.definition: aduncitās ātis, f aduncus, hookedness: rostrorum.

aduncus.definition: 'ad-uncus adj., bent inwards, hooked: unguis: nasus, aquiline, H.: ferrum, barbed, O.'

adurgeo.definition: ad-urgeō —, —, ēre, to pursue closely: volantem Remis, H.

aduro.definition: ad-ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere, to set on fire, kindle, scorch, parch, burn, singe: hoc, T.: panis adustus, scorched, H.: ossa flammis, H.: sine gemitu aduruntur, endure burning.—To nip, freeze, blast: ne frigus adurat, V.: …

adusque.definition: ad-ūsque or ad ūsque praep.—Poet., all the way to, as far as: columnas, V.—As adv.: ad usque, quā, etc., wherever, O.

adustus.definition: adūstus adj. P. of aduro with comp, sunburnt, brown: hominum color, L.: alqd adustioris coloris, L.

advecticius.definition: advectīcius (not -tītius), adj. adveho, imported: vinum, S.

advecto.definition: advectō —, —, āre, freq. adveho, to keep bringing, import continually: copiam, Ta.

advectus.definition: advectus ūs, m adveho, a bringing hither: deae, Ta.

adveho.definition: ad - vehō vēxī, vectus, ere, to bring hither, carry to, conduct: ex agris Romam: sive diem advexerit annus, H.—Pass, to be brought, arrive: ista quae advecta est, T.: citato equo advectus, rode up at full speed, L.: c…

advelo.definition: ad-vēlō —, —, āre, to veil, wreathe: tempora lauro, V.

advena.definition: advena ae, m and f ad + BA-, VEN-, a stranger, foreigner, immigrant: advena anus, T.: possessor agelli, V.—Fig.: in nostrā patriā advenae, i. e. unskilled in our own department. — Strange, foreign, alien: exercitus, V…

advenio.definition: ad-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come to, reach, arrive at: Delphos: huc, T.: in provinciam: classem adveniens profligaverim, by my mere arrival, Cs.: mihi advenienti dextram porrigere, at my approach: urbem, V.— With s…

adventicius.definition: adventīcius adj. advenio, foreign, strange, accidental: auxilia.— Foreign, extraordinary: pecunia: fructus, incidental, L.

advento.definition: adventō —, —, āre, intens. advenio, to advance, press forward, march on, approach: Caesar adventare nuntiabatur, Cs.: adventans senectus: ad Italiam: Romam, S.: adventante deā, at her coming, V.: adventante urbi clade…

adventus.definition: adventus ūs (gen. adventi, T.), m ad + BA-, VEN-, a coming, approach, arrival: meus, S.: legionum, Cs.: nocturnus ad urbem: in urbem sociorum: consulis Romam, L.: nisi eius adventus appropinquasset, N.: Huius in adven…

adversarius.definition: adversārius (advor-) adj. adversor, opposite, hostile, contrary: duces: multitudinis temeritati: rebus nox, unfavorable, Cs.: oratori opinio, injurious. — As substt. m. and f an opponent, adversary, enemy: acerrimus: …

adversatrix.definition: adversātrīx (advor-) īcis, f adversator, an opponent: in eā re mihi, T.

adversio.definition: adversiō ōnis, f adverto, direction, employment: animi.

adversor.definition: adversor (advor-) sātus, ārī, dep. adversus, to resist, withstand, oppose: adversante naturā: par in adversandum, i. e. able to resist, L.: legi: huius libidini.—With quo minus, C.

adversum1.definition: adversum (advor-) adv. and praep., see 2 adversus.

adversum2.definition: adversum ī, n the opposite direction: hic ventus adversum tenet Athenis proficiscentibus, N.: in adversum Romani subiere, directly to the hill, L.— Fig., opposed, contrary, hostile, adverse, unfavorable, unpropitious:…

adversum3.definition: adversum ī, n misfortune, calamity, disaster: uti Advorsa eius per te tecta sient, T.: nihil adversi exspectare: si quando adversa vocarent, if misfortune should require, V.

adversus1.definition: adversus (advor-) adj. with sup. P. of adverto, turned towards, fronting, facing, before, in front: intueri solem: adverso sole, in the sunlight, V.: dentes, front-teeth: collis, Cs.: Ibat in adversum hostem, O.: adve…

adversus2.definition: adversus ī, m an enemy, opponent: vir populi partium, an opponent of the democrats, S. — 2.

adversus3.definition: adversus or adversum (advor-) adv. and praep. adverto. I. As adv., opposite, in opposition: advorsum ire, to go to meet (him), T.: adversus resistere, N. — II. As praep. with acc, opposite to, before, facing: paries a…

adverto.definition: advertō (advortō) tī, sus, ere, to turn to, turn towards, direct: In partem lumina, O.: agmen urbi, V.: terris proram, V.: classem in portum, L.: hue carinam, O.: Scythicas advertitur oras, steers to, O.: proram, to t…

advesperascit.definition: ad-vesperāscit —, ere, impers, it approaches evening, is twilight: cum advesperascere<*>.

advigilo.definition: advigilō āvī, —, āre, to watch, be watchful: ad custodiam ignis: nepoti, Tb.: si advigilaveris, T.

advocata.definition: advocāta ae, f advoco, one called to aid, a supporter: non desiderat fortitudo advocatam iracundiam.

advocatio.definition: advocātiō ōnis, f advoco, a summoning as counsel: maximarum rerum advocationes, i. e. consultations: in advocationibus, i. e. as an advocate. —The advocates, counsel, bar, body of pleaders: ea: ingens, L. — A delay fo…

advocatus.definition: advocātus ī, m advoco, one called to aid.— In law, a friend who supports a party in a trial, an attendant, adviser: adesse advocatos nobis, T.: in advocati loco: adesse sine advocatis, i. e. without his guard.—A plead…

advoco.definition: ad-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call, summon, invite: contionem: complures senatorii ordinis, Cs.: eo senatum, S.: populum ad tribunum, L.: Ut noris quibus advoceris Gaudiis, to what pleasures you are invited, H.: viros in…

advolatus.definition: advolātus ūs, m advolo, an approach by flying: tristi advolatu (once), C. poet.

advolo.definition: ad-volō āvī, ātus, āre, to fly to, fly towards: avis ad aves. — To hasten to: Larino Romam: classem advolituram esse, Cs.: Aeneae, V.: ad urbem: rostra.

advolvo.definition: ad-volvō volvī, volūtus, ere, to roll to, roll towards, bring by rolling: congesta robora focis, V.: ornos montibus, from the mountains, V.— To fall prostrate before: genibus omnium, L.

adytum.definition: adytum ī, n, a)/duton. — Usu. plur, the inmost recess, holiest place: adyti incola, H.: penetralia, V.: ima, the inmost part of a tomb, V.

aedicula.definition: aedicula ae, f dim. (aedes), a small temple, chapel, niche, C., L.— Plur, a small dwelling, T., C.

aedificatio.definition: aedificātiō ōnis, f aedifico, the process of building: intermissa.—A building, structure, edifice: omnis.—Plur: privatae, Ta.

aedificatiuncula.definition: aedificātiuncula ae, f dim. aedificatio, a little building.

aedificator.definition: aedificātor ōris, m aedifico, a builder: mundi.—One fond of building: nemo minus, N.

aedificium.definition: aedificium ī, n aedifico, a building, edifice, structure: aedificiis incensis, Cs.: exstruere.

aedifico.definition: aedificō āvī, ātus, āre aedifex; aedes + 2 FAC-, to build, erect a building: ad aestūs vitandos, Cs.: aedificandi descriptio, plan: diruit, aedificat, H.—To build, construct, erect: urbem: naves, Cs.: alia (aedificia)…

aedilicius.definition: aedīlīcius (not -tius), adj. aedilis, of an aedile: munus.— As subst, m., one who has been an aedile.

aedilis.definition: aedīlis is, m aedes, a commissioner of buildings, aedile, magistrate for public works.

aedilitas.definition: aedīlitās ātis, f aedīlis, the office of an aedile, aedileship: aedilitatem petere: aedilitate fungi.

aedis.definition: aedis or aedēs is (acc plur. usu aedīs), f AID-, a dwelling of the gods, temple, sanctuary (usu. a single edifice without partitions, while templum is a larger structure): Minervae: aedīs sacras incendere: in aede son…

aedituus.definition: aedituus ī, m aedes + 2 TV-, a custodian of a temple, sacristan, C.: qualīs Aedituos habeat virtus, i. e. poets, H.

aeger.definition: aeger gra, grum, adj., unwell, ill, sick, diseased, suffering, feeble: uxor, T.: homines morbo: aegro corpore esse: volneribus, N.: pedibus, S.: anhelitus, shortness of breath, V.: sues, V.: seges, V. —As subst, a sic…

aegis.definition: aegis idis, f the shield of Jupiter, with the head of Medusa borne by Minerva, V., H. — A shield, defence, O.

aegre.definition: aegrē adv. with comp. aegrius, and sup. aegerrimē aeger, painfully, distressingly: audire, T.: aegrest, it is annoying, T.: ferre, to feel distress.— With difficulty, hardly, scarcely: divelli: bellum sumi facile, aeg…

aegresco.definition: aegrēscō —, —, ere aeger, to fall sick: sollicitudine, Ta. — To grow worse, be exasperated: violentia medendo, V.

aegrimonia.definition: aegrimōnia ae, f aeger, anxiety, trouble, C., H.

aegritudo.definition: aegritūdō dinis, f aeger, sickness, grief, affliction, melancholy: in animo: ira et aegritudo permixta, S.: acrior: lenior.

aegrotatio.definition: aegrōtātiō ōnis, f aegroto, sickness, disease: in corpore: animi, a morbid state.

aegroto.definition: aegrōtō āvī, —, āre aegrotus, to be sick, languish, pine: graviter: morbo, H.—Of cattle, H.— To suffer: animus aegrotat: animi vitio, H.

aegrotus.definition: aegrōtus adj. aeger, sick, diseased: corpus, H.: leo, H.—As subst, a sick person, invalid: consilia aegrotis damus, T.: aegroto, dum anima est, spes esse dicitur: animus, T., C.: res p.

aelinos.definition: aelinos ī, m, ai)/linos, a dirge, O.

aemulatio.definition: aemulātiō ōnis, f aemulor, rivalry, emulation, competition: inter alquos, N.: gloriae, L.: honoris, Ta.: vitiosa.—Plur, jealousies, C.

aemulator.definition: aemulātor ōris, m aemulor, a zealous imitator, Catonis.

aemulatus.definition: aemulātus ūs, m rivalry, jealousy, Ta. — Plur., Ta.

aemulor.definition: aemulor ātus, ārī aemulus, to rival, vie with, emulate, strive to excel: eius instituta: Agamemnonem, N.: studia, L.: virtutes, Ta.—To envy, be jealous of: iis qui, etc.: mecum, L.: inter se, Ta.

aemulus.definition: aemulus adj. 2 IC-, AIC-, striving earnestly after, emulating, rivalling, vying with, emulous: laudis: studiorum: itinerum Herculis, L. — Envious, jealous, grudging, malicious: Triton, V.— As subst, a rival: alqm tamq…

aeneus.definition: aēneüs (ahēn-) adj. aes, of copper, of bronze: galea: aë neus ut stes, i. e. in a statue, H.: proles, the age of brass, O.: hic murus aë neus esto, a bulwark (of character), H.

aenigma.definition: aenigma atis, n, ai)/nigma, a figure, allegory, C.

aenipes.definition: aēnipēs (ahēn-) edis, adj. aēnus + pes, bronze-footed, O.

aenus.definition: aēnus (ahēn-) adj. aes, of copper, of bronze: thorax, V.: lux, lustre, V.—As subst n., a brazen vessel, kettle: Tyrium, a dye-kettle, O. — Plur., for warming water, V.—Strong, firm: manus, H.

aequabilis.definition: aequābilis e, adj. with comp. aequo, like, similar, equal, uniform: ius: praedae partitio: satio. — Consistent, equable, constant, unvarying: nihil eā iurisdictione aequabilius: fortuna, without vicissitude: pulveris …

aequabilitas.definition: aequābilitās ātis, f aequabilis, equality, uniformity, evenness: motūs: vitae.—Fig., equity, impartiality: decernendi: iuris. — Of style, uniformity: orationis.

aequabiliter.definition: aequābiliter adv. with comp. aequabilis, equally: praedam dispertire: frumentum emere ab civitatibus.—Indiscriminately: in rem p., in privatos ... inruebat.—Uniformly, unvaryingly: mare conglobatur: omnes erant eius m…

aequaevus.definition: 'aequaevus adj. aequus + aevum, of equal age: rex, V.'

aequalis.definition: aequālis e, adj. with comp. aequo, equal, like, even, on a par: virtutes inter se: eis genus, eloquentia, aetas aequalia, S.—Of the same age, equally old: chorus aequalis Dryadum, V. — As subst, a contemporary, fellow…

aequalitas.definition: aequālitās ātis, f aequalis, equality, similarity, likeness: fraterna: vestra. — Equality of civil rights, Ta.

aequaliter.definition: aequāliter adv. with comp. aequalis, evenly, equably: declivis, uniformly, Cs.: ingrediens: sternere undam, O.—Equally, equitably: distribuere: aequalius duci parebant, Ta.

aequanimitas.definition: aequanimitās ātis, f aequus + animus, good-will, kindness, T.

aequatio.definition: aequātiō ōnis, f aequo, an equal distribution, community: bonorum: iuris, L.

aequatus.definition: aequātus adj. P. of aequo, level, levelled, even: agri planities: (mensam) tersere, O.: aequatis procedere velis, with even sails, i. e. before the wind, V.: aequatis rostris, side by side, V.

aeque.definition: aequē adv. with comp. and sup. aequus, equally, in like manner, just as, in an equal degree, to the same extent: Utin omnes eadem aeque studeant, T.: honore non aeque omnes egent: aeque calidus animis et cursibus acer…

aequilibritas.definition: aequilībritās ātis, f aequus + libra, equipoise.

aequinoctialis.definition: aequinoctiālis e, adj. aequinoctium, equinoctial: caeli furor, Ct.

aequinoctium.definition: aequinoctium ī, n aequus + nox, the equinox: dies aequinoctii: vernum, L.

aequipero.definition: aequiperō āvī, ātus, āre aequus + par, to compare, liken: cum fratre gloriam: Iovis equis dictatorem, L.—To equal, come up to, rival: alqm labore, N.: urbem dignitate, N.: voce magistrum, V.

aequitas.definition: aequitās ātis, f aequus, uniformity, evenness; with animi, calmness, repose, equability, equanimity: animi in morte, calmness: novi moderationem animi tui et aequitatem: ut animi aequitate plebem contineant, Cs.: mira…

aequo.definition: aequō āvī, ātus, āre aequus, to make equal, equalize: suas opes cum potentissimis aequari, Cs.: numerum (corporum) cum navibus, V.: fortunam animis, L.: tecta caelo, raise, V.: illi ... amorem, returns equal love, V.:…

aequor.definition: aequor oris, n aequus, an even surface, level: camporum aequora: campi, V.: Libyci aequoris harenae, V.—In ending a long poem: inmensum spatiis confecimus aequor, V. — Esp., the sea, ocean: Aegaeum, O.: ingens, H.: sa…

aequoreus.definition: 'aequoreus adj. aequor, of the sea, marine: rex, Neptune, O.: Britanni, islanders, O.: genus, i. e. fish, V.'

aequum.definition: aequum ī, n a plain, level: in aequo campi, L.—Fairness, justice: utilitas iusti prope mater et aequi, H.: eas (iniurias) gravius aequo habere, to feel too deeply, S.: potus largius aequo, H.: aequo violentior, O.

aequus.definition: aequus adj. with comp. and sup. 2 IC-, AIC-, even, plain, level, flat: locus: aequiore loco constiterat, Cs.: campus, V. — Equal: ex provinciā aequam partem sumere: sequitur non passibus aequis, V.: Abietibus iuvenes …

aer.definition: āēr āeris, acc. āera, m, a)h/r, the air, atmosphere, sky, esp. the lower air: nudus in aere, in the open air: aera vincere summum arboris, i. e. the summit, V.—A mist, vapor: densus, H.: obscurus, V.—The weather: cras…

aeraria.definition: aerāria ae, f aerarius, a mine.

aerarium.definition: aerārium ī, n aerarius, part of the temple of Saturn at Rome, in which the public treasure was kept, the treasury: referre (pecuniam) in aerarium: pecunia data tibi ex aerario.—Hence, the public treasure, finances: cu…

aerarius1.definition: aerārius adj. aes, of copper, of bronze, made of copper; hence, of copper money: fabula, a twopenny story. — Of mines: structurae, Cs.— Of money, pecuniary: ratio, the rate of exchange, current value of coin. — Of the…

aerarius2.definition: aerārius ī, m a resident who pays a polltax, but cannot vote nor hold office. The censors could degrade citizens to this class; hence, aerarium alqm facere, L.: alqm in aerariis relinquere: qui te ex aerariis exemit.

aeratus.definition: aerātus adj. aes, of bronze: cuspis, O. — Fitted with bronze: lecti, having bronze feet: navis, with a bronze beak, Cs.: acies, in armor, V. —Supplied with money, rich (once): tribuni.

aereus.definition: 'aereus adj. aes, of copper, of bronze: signa, L.: clipeus, Cu.: vectes, V.: clipeus, V.: puppis, i. e. with bronze beak, V.'

aerifer.definition: 'aerifer fera, ferum, adj., bearing bronze, i. e. carrying cymbals (once): manus, O.'

aeripes.definition: aeripēs edīs, adj. aes + pes, with feet of bronze: cerva, V.: tauri, O.

aerugo.definition: aerūgō inis, f aes, rust of copper, verdigris, C.—Rusty gold, Iu.—Poet., a corroding passion: mera, envy, H.: animos aerugo Cum imbuerit, avarice, H.

aerumna.definition: aerumna ae, f cf. īra, toil, hardship, distress, trouble, tribulation: alqm expedire his aerumnis, T.: rem p. servare aerumnā: multae, H.: mors aerumnarum requies, S.

aerumnosus.definition: aerumnōsus adj. with sup, full of trouble, miserable, wretched, distressed: salum: pater: felix et aerumnosus: aerumnosissima mulier.
