anatocismus.definition: anatocismus ī, m, a)natokismo/s, interest upon interest, compound interest.

anceps.definition: anceps cipitis, abl. cipitī, adj. an- (for ambi-) + CAP-, that has two heads, two-headed: Ianus, O.: acumen, two-peaked, O.—Meton., double, twosided: securis, two-edged, O.: bestiae quasi ancipites in utrāque sede viv…

ancile.definition: ancīle is (gen plur. -ilium, Ta., once, -iliorum, H.), n a small oval shield, V.; usu. the shield said to have fallen from heaven in the reign of Numa, and on the preservation of which the prosperity of Rome was decla…

ancilla.definition: 'ancilla ae, f dim. ancula, a female attendant, a maid-servant, handmaid: aere empta, T.: ancillarum comitatus: mulier ancilla, S.'

ancillaris.definition: ancillāris e, adj. ancilla, of a female servant: artificium, a handmaid's service.

ancillula.definition: ancillula ae, f dim. ancilla, a young female slave, handmaid: ex Aethiopiā , T.—Fig.: eloquentiae.

ancora.definition: ancora ae, f, a)/gkura, an anchor: dente Ancora fundabat naves, V.: ancoram iacere, to cast anchor, Cs.: tenere navem in ancoris, N.: ad ancoram constitit, lay at anchor, Cs.: tollere, to weigh anchor, Cs.: praecidere…

ancorale.definition: ancorāle is, n ancora, an anchor-cable: ancoralia incidunt, L.

ancorarius.definition: ancorārius adj. ancora, of an anchor: funes, cables, Cs.

andabata.definition: andabata ae, m a gladiator, who fought blindfold.

androgynus.definition: androgynus ī, m, a)ndro/gunos, a man woman, hermaphrodite.

anellus.definition: ānellus (ann-) ī, m dim. anulus, a little ring, H.

anethum.definition: anēthum ī, n, a)/nhthon, dill, anise: bene olens, V.

anfractus.definition: ānfrāctus ūs, m am- (for ambi-) + FRAG-, a recurving, turning, bending round: quae (figura) nihil incisum anfractibus habere potest: solis, a circuit.—Esp., a tortuous way, circuitous route: si nullus anfractus interc…

ango.definition: angō —, —, ere ANG-, to draw close, press tight, squeeze, compress, throttle, choke: sanguine guttur, V.: Tussis sues angit, V. — Fig., to torment, torture, vex, tease, trouble: cura angit hominem, T.: angebat spiritu…

angor.definition: angor ōris, m ANG-, a strangling, suffocation: gens aestu et angore vexata (i. e. by dust and ashes), L. — Fig., anguish, torment, trouble: ut differt anxietas ab angore: pro amico capiendus: confici angoribus, by mel…

anguicomus.definition: 'anguicomus (quadrisyl.), adj. anguis + coma, with snaky hair (poet.): Gorgon, O.'

anguiculus.definition: anguiculus ī, m dim. anguis, a small serpent.

anguifer.definition: 'anguifer (trisyl.), era, erum, adj. anguis + FER-, serpent-bearing (poet.): caput, O.: Gorgo, Pr.'

anguigena.definition: anguigena ae, m anguis + GEN-, engendered of a serpent, i. e. sprung from dragons' teeth, O.

anguilla.definition: anguilla ae, f dim. anguis, an eel, Iu.

anguineus.definition: 'anguineus adj., of serpents, snaky: Gorgonis comae, O.'

anguinus.definition: anguīnus (trisyl.), adj. anguis, of serpents, snaky: capillus, Ct.

anguipes.definition: anguipēs (trisyl.), edis, adj. anguis + pes, serpent-footed (poet.); of giants, O.

anguis.definition: anguis (disyl.), is (abl. angue; rarely anguī), m and f ANG-, a serpent, snake: os cinctum anguibus: tortus, O.: cane peius et angui vitare, i. e. most anxiously, H.—Esp., in fable as an emblem: of terror, the snaky h…

angulatus.definition: angulātus adj. angulus, with corners, angular: corpuscula.

angulus.definition: angulus ī, m 1 AC-, an angle, corner: ad pares angulos ferri, at right angles: huius lateris alter, Cs.: extremus, the farthest corner, O.: proximus, H. — Meton., a secret place, nook, corner, lurking-place: in angulu…

anguste.definition: angustē adv. with comp. and sup. angustus, narrowly, within a narrow space, closely: sedere, in close quarters: angustius se habere: angustissime Pompeium continere, Cs. — Fig., concisely: scribere.—Meton., pinchingly…

angustia.definition: angustia ae (sing. very rare), and angustiae, ārum, f angustus, narrowness, straitness: itineris, Cs.: loci, S. — Meton., a narrow place, narrow part, neck, defile, strait: Graeciae: angustiae saltibus inclusae, pass,…

angusto.definition: angustō —, —, āre angustus, to make narrow, straiten: iter corporum acervis, Ct.

angustum.definition: angustum ī, n angustus, a narrow place: viarum, V.: res adducta in angustum, brought into narrow limits.—Fig., a critical condition, embarrassment, difficulty, danger: rem esse in angusto vidit, Cs.: in angustum venire.

angustus.definition: angustus adj. with comp. and sup. ANG-, narrow, strait, contracted: iter, S.: fines, Cs.: rima, H.: mare, a strait: angustissima portus, Cs.— Fig., short, brief: dies, O.: spiritus, breathing.— Needy, pinching, stinti…

anhelitus.definition: anhēlitus ūs, m anhelo, a difficulty of breathing, panting, puffing, deep breathing: a lasso ore, O.: vini, drunken reviling: sublimis, H.: aeger, V.—Meton., an exhalation, vapor: terrae.

anhelo.definition: anhēlō āvī, ātus, āre anhelus.—Intrans, to breathe with difficulty, gasp, pant, puff: confugere anhelantem domum, T.: anhelabat sub vomere taurus, O.—Meton., of fire, to roar, crash: fornacibus ignis anhelat, V.—Trans…

anhelus.definition: anhēlus adj. see AN-, out of breath, short of breath, panting, puffing, gasping (poet.): senes, V.: cursus, that cause panting, O.: tussis, V.

anicula.definition: 'anicula ae, f dim. anus, a little old woman, granny, T.: minime suspiciosa.'

anilis.definition: anīlis e, adj. anus, of an old woman: voltus, V.: passus, O.—Old-womanish, anile, silly: ineptiae: fabellae, H.

anilitas.definition: anīlitās ātis, f anilis, the old age of a woman: cana, Ct.

aniliter.definition: anīliter adv. anilis, like an old woman: dicere.

anima.definition: anima ae, f AN-, air, a current of air, breeze, breath, wind: impellunt animae lintea, H.: ignes animaeque, V. — Esp., the air utrum (animus) sit ignis, an anima: semina terrarum animaeque, V.—Breath: animam compressi…

animabilis.definition: animābilis e, adj. anima, enlivening, animating: natura (of the air; al. animalis).

animadversio.definition: animadversiō ōnis, f animadverto, investigation, inquiry: nostra in civem est, L.—Perception, notice, observation: hoc totum est animadversionis: excitanda animadversio, ut ne quid temere agamus, self-inspection.—Repr…

animadversor.definition: animadversor ōris, m animadverto, a censor (once): vitiorum.

animadverto.definition: animadvertō or -vortō or (older) animum advertō (constr. as one word), tī, sus, ere animum + adverto, to direct the mind, give attention to, attend to, consider, regard, observe: tuam rem, T.: eadem in pace: sed anima…

animal.definition: animal ālis, abl. animālī, n anima, a living being, animal: omne: providum: perfidiosum: sanctius his animal, O.: Cum prorepserunt primis animalia terris, H.

animalis.definition: animālis e, adj. anima, of air, aerial: natura. — Of life, vital: cibus. — Animate, living: intellegentia: exemplum.

animans.definition: animāns antis, adj. P. of 1 animo, animate, living: deos.—Subst, a living being, animal: animantium genera. — Of man: haud petit Quemquam animantem, H.

animatio.definition: animātiō ōnis, f 1 animo, an animating.— Meton., a living being (once).

animatus.definition: animātus adj. P. of 2 animo, disposed, inclined, minded: sic ut, etc.: ut in amicum: insulae bene, favorable, N.: animatus melius quam paratus.

animo1.definition: animō āvī, ātus, āre anima, to enliven, quicken, animate: stellae divinis animatae mentibus.—Poet.: guttas in angues, O.

animo2.definition: animō āvī, ātus, āre animus, to dispose, inspirit: ita pueros: Mattiaci solo ac caelo acrius animantur, are inspirited, Ta.

animose.definition: animōsē adv. animosus, spiritedly, courageously, eagerly: id fecerunt: vivere, independently.

animosus1.definition: animōsus adj. anima, full of air, airy: guttura, through which the breath passes, O.—Full of life: signa, Pr.—Violent: Eurus, V.

animosus2.definition: animōsus adj. with comp. animus, full of courage, bold, spirited, undaunted: pugnis: animosior senectus quam adulescentia, shows more courage: (equorum) pectus, V.: Rebus angustis animosus appare, H.—Proud: parens, vo…

animula.definition: animula ae, f dim. anima, a breeze.—A bit of life: mihi quidquam animulae instillare.

animus.definition: animus ī, m AN-, the rational soul (cf. anima, the physical life): humanus: Corpus animum praegravat, H.: deos sparsisse animos in corpora humana: discessus animi a corpore: permanere animos arbitramur. — Fig., of bel…

annalis1.definition: annālis e, adj. annus, relating to a year: lex, which fixed the age required for office.

annalis2.definition: annālis is, abl. annalī, m 1 annalis; sc. liber, a record of events, chronicles, annals.—The Pontifex Maximus each year used to record public events on tablets, called Annales Maximi; hence historical works are called…

anniculus.definition: 'anniculus adj. annus, of a year, yearling: virgo, N.'

anniversarius.definition: anniversārius annus + verto, returning every year, annual, yearly: festi dies: arma, annual wars, L.

annona.definition: annōna ae, f annus, the year's produce: vectigal ex salariā annonā , out of the annual supply, L. — Means of subsistence, provisions, corn, grain, crop: Tum annona carast, is dear, T.: caritas annonae, scarcity: perfu…

annosus.definition: annōsus adj. annus, full of years, aged, old: anus, O.: bracchia (ulmi), V.: ornus, V.: cornix, H.

annotinus.definition: annōtinus adj. annus; cf. diutinus, a year old, of last year: naves, Cs.

annus.definition: annus ī, m 1 AC-, a year (orig. ten months, from Martius to December; after Numa, twelve): annos sexaginta natus es, T.: se annum posse vivere: ad annum octogesimum pervenire, N.: annos habere quattuor, to be four yea…

annuus.definition: annuus adj. annus, of a year, lasting a year: tempus: qui (magistratus) creatur annuus, Cs.: reges, N.: cultura, H.: labor, a whole year's work: signorum commutationes, during the year.—Yearly, annual: Sacra, V.

anquiro.definition: anquīrō sīvī, sītus, ere am- (for ambi-) + quaero, to seek on all sides, look about, search after: aliquem: omnia, quae sunt, etc.— Fig., to inquire diligently, examine into: alqd: conducat id necne: quid valeat id, a…

ansa.definition: ānsa ae, f a handle, haft: canthari, V.: poculi, O.—The catch of a shoe-string, H.—Fig., an occasion, opportunity: reprehensionis: sermonis ansae, clews: ad reprehendendum.

anser.definition: ānser eris, m cf. Engl. gander, a goose; sacred to Juno, C., L., II.

ante.definition: ante adv. and praep. ANT-. I. Adv., of space, before, in front, forwards: ante aut post pugnandi ordo, L.: positum ante pullum Sustulit, served, H.: non ante, sed retro.—Usu. of time, before, previously: nonne oportui…

antea.definition: anteā (archaic antideā, L.), adv., before, earlier, formerly, aforetime, previously: antea, cum equester ordo iudicaret: ac fuit antea tempus, cum, Cs.: cum antea semper factiosus fuisset, N.: si numquam antea cogitas…

antecapio.definition: ante-capiō cēpī, ceptus, ere, to obtain before, receive before: antecepta informatio, an innate idea.—Esp., to seize beforehand, preoccupy: quae bello usui forent, S.—To anticipate: noctem, S.: ea omnia luxu, S.

antecedens.definition: antecēdēns entis, adj. P. of antecedo, foregoing, preceding: hora.—In philosophy, the antecedent: causa. — Plur. as subst, the premises (of reasoning).

antecedo.definition: ante-cēdō essī, —, ere, to go before, get the start, precede: ad explorandum, L.: antecedentem scelestum, H.: magnis itineribus, Cs.: legiones.— Fig., to precede: si huic rei illa antecedit, is a logical condition of:…

antecello.definition: ante-cellō —, —, ere 2 CEL-, to be prominent, distinguish oneself, excel, surpass, be superior: longe ceteris: ubertate agrorum terris: omnibus gloriā: vestrae exercitationi ad honorem, with respect to honor: perigrin…

antecessio.definition: antecessiō ōnis, f antecedo, a going before, preceding.— Meton., an antecedent.

antecursor.definition: antecursor ōris, m antecurro.—Prop., a forerunner; only plur, the vanguard, pioneers, Cs.

anteeo.definition: ante-eō īvī or iī, —, īre (anteit, disyl., H., O.; anteirent, trisyl., V.; anteat, O.; antībō, Ta.; antissent, Ta.; antisse, Ta.), to go before, precede: strenuus anteis, H.: ubi anteire primores vident, L.: Te semper…

antefero.definition: ante-ferō tulī, lātum, ferre, to bear in front, carry before: quod fasces anteferrentur, Cs. — Fig., of estimation, to place before, prefer: alqd commodis suis: pacem bello: te Grais, H.

antefixus.definition: ante-fīxus adj. ante + figo, fastened before: truncis arborum antefixa ora, i. e. skulls, Ta. — Plur n. as subst, little images on the front of a house or temple, L.

antegredior.definition: antegredior essus, ī, dep. ante + gradior, to go before, precede: solem. — In time: cum antegressa est honestas: causae antegressae.

antehabeo.definition: ante-habeō —, —, ēre, to prefer: quieta turbidis, Ta.: incredibilia veris, Ta.

antehac.definition: ante-hāc (disyl., H.), adv. of time, before this time, before now, formerly, hitherto: fecit, T.: antehac uti solebat, etc.: antehac nefas (erat) ... dum, etc., H.—Before that time, earlier, previously: saepe antehac …

antelucanus.definition: antelūcānus adj. ante + lux, before light, before dawn: tempus: cenae, lasting all night.

antemeridianus.definition: ante-merīdiānus adj., before mid-day, of the forenoon: sermo: ambulatio.

antemna.definition: 'antemna or antenna ae, f ante + TA-, TEN-, a ship''s yard: antemnas ad malos destinare, Cs.: antemnae gemunt, H.: cornua antemnarum, V.'

anteoccupatio.definition: ante-occupātiō ōnis, f—In rhet., an anticipation (of objections).

antepes.definition: ante-pēs edis, m the forefoot, C. (poet.).

antepilanus.definition: ante-pīlānus ī, m a soldier of the first two ranks, in front of the triarii, L.

antepono.definition: ante - pōnō posuī, positus, ere, to set before: propugnacula anteposita, Ta.: equitum locos sedilibus, Ta.—Fig., to prefer, value above: amicitiam omnibus rebus: gloria formulis anteponenda est: gloriam potentiae, S.—…

antes.definition: antēs īum, m rows (of vines), V.

antesignanus.definition: ante-sīgnānus ī, m ante + signum, a leader in battle: in acie.—Plur m. as subst., the soldiers who fought in front of the standards, Cs., L.

antestor.definition: antestor ātus, ārī, dep. an- (for ambi-) + testor, in law, to call as a witness, summon to testify (the summoner said, licet antestari? the summoned offered his ear to be touched): Licet antestari? Ego vero Oppono aur…

antevenio.definition: ante-veniō vēnī, ventus, īre, to come before, get the start of, anticipate: exercitum, S.: consilia (hostium), thwart, S.: ne ... Anteveni, V.—Fig., to exceed, surpass, excel: per virtutem nobilitatem, S.

anteverto.definition: ante-vertō (-vor-) tī, —, ere, to take a place before, go before, precede: tum antevertens, tum subsequens.—Fig., to anticipate: huic, T.: mihi. —To prefer, place before: omnibus consiliis antevertendum existimavit, u…

anthias.definition: anthias ae, m an unknown sea-fish, O.

anticipatio.definition: anticipātiō ōnis, f anticipo, a preconception, preconceived notion: deorum.

anticipo.definition: anticipō āvī, ātus, āre ante + CAP-, to take before, anticipate: rei molestiam: anticipata via est, travelled more quickly, O.

anticus.definition: antīcus adj. ANT-, in front, foremost: pars; see also antiquus.

antidotum.definition: antidotum ī, n, a)nti/doton, a remedy against poison, Ph.

antiquaria.definition: antīquāria ae, f antiquus, a female antiquarian (once), Iu.

antiquarius.definition: antiquarius ī, m an antiquarian, Ta., O.

antique.definition: antīquē adv. with comp. antiquus, like the ancients, in the old fashion: dicere, H.: antiquius permutatione mercium uti, the old method of barter, Ta.

antiquitas.definition: antīquitās ātis, f antiquus, age, antiquity: generis. — Ancient time, antiquity: factum ex omni antiquitate proferre.—Ancient events, the history of ancient times, antiquity: tenenda est omnis antiquitas: antiquitatis…

antiquitus.definition: antīquitus adv. antiquus, in former times, of old, anciently, long ago: Belgas Rhenum antiquitus traductos, Cs.: tectum antiquitus constitutum, N.: insita pertinacia familiae, L.: panicum paratum, long before, Cs.

antiquo.definition: antīquō āvī, ātus, āre antiquus, of a bill, to reject, not to pass: legem antiquari passus est: legem tribūs antiquarunt (opp. iuserunt), L.

antiquus.definition: antīquus (-īcus) adj. with comp. and sup. ante, ancient, former, of old times: tua duritia, former severity, T.: causa antiquior memoriā tuā : patria, L.: urbs, V.: antiquae leges et mortuae. —Plur m. as subst, the an…

antistes.definition: antistes itis, m and f ante + STA-, an overseer of a temple, high-priest, priest of a rite or a god: caerimoniarum: sacri eius, L.: Iovis, N.: sacrorum, Iu. — Fem. (for antistita): adsiduae templi antistites, unremitt…

antistita.definition: 'antistita ae, f antistes, a female superintendent (of a temple or worship), high-priestess: fani: Phoebi, O.'

antisto.definition: antistō (not antes-) stetī, —, āre ante + sto, to stand before, only fig., to excel, surpass, be superior: quanto antistaret eloquentia innocentiae, N.: si (quaeritur) ratio ... Pompeius antistat: alcui aliquā re.

antrum.definition: antrum ī, n, a)/ntron, a cave, cavern, grotto (poet.): gelida antra, V.: sylvestria, O.: Pierium, H.—Meton., a hollow: exesae arboris, V.: clausum (of a sedan), Iu.

anularius.definition: ānulārius ī, m anulus, a maker of rings.

anulus.definition: ānulus ī, m dim. 1 ānus, a ring, finger-ring, seal-ring, signet-ring: de digito anulum detraho, T.: gemmati anuli, L.: sigilla anulo imprimere: equestris (as worn only by knights), H.: anulum invenit (i. e. eques fact…

anus1.definition: ānus ī, m AS-.—Prop., a ring; hence, the fundament.

anus2.definition: anus ūs (rarely -uis, T.), f an old woman, matron, old wife, old maid: prudens, H.: pia, O.: Iunonis anus templique sacerdos, aged priestess, V.: delira. — Esp., a female soothsayer, sibyl, H. —As adj., old: cerva anu…

anxie.definition: ānxiē adv. anxius, anxiously: ferre alqd, S.

anxietas.definition: ānxietās ātis, f anxius, anxiety, solicitude: animi, O.: perpetua, Iu.

anxifer.definition: ānxifer fera, ferum, adj. anxius + FER-, bringing anxiety, distressing: curae, C. poet.

anxitudo.definition: ānxitūdō dinis, f anxius, trouble, distress.

anxius.definition: ānxius adj. ANG-, of a state or mood, anxious, troubled, solicitous: nec, qui anxii, semper anguntur: mentes, H.: suam vicem, magis quam eius, L.: animi, S.: animo, S.: erga Seianum, Ta.: de curis, Cu.: pro regno, O.:…

apage.definition: 'apage interj., a)/page, away with thee! begone! away! off with! (comic and colloq.): apage te, T.: apage sis, T.'

apeliotes.definition: apēliōtēs ae, m, a)phliw/ths, the east wind, Ct.

aper.definition: aper aprī, m 2 AP-, a wild boar ingens: spumans, V.—As a delicacy, H.—Prov. of folly: liquidis inmisi fontibus apros, V.

aperio.definition: aperiō eruī, ertus, īre ab + 2 PAR-, to uncover, lay bare: caput: aperto pectore, with bared breast, O.: ingulo aperto, with his throat cut, O.: partūs, bring to light, H.: apertae pectora matres, with bared breasts, …

aperte.definition: apertē adv. with comp. and sup. apertus, openly, manifestly: vincere, in open fight, O.: odisse: alqd venale ostendere, without disguise, H. — Of language, without reserve, plainly, clearly: tibi fabulari, T.: apertiu…

apertus.definition: apertus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of aperio, without covering, uncovered: magna corporis pars, Cs.: locus: naves, not decked: caelo invectus aperto, unclouded, V.: aperta serena prospicere, V.—Unclosed, open, not sh…

apex.definition: apex icis, m 1 AP-, the extreme end, point, summit, top: lauri, V.: montis, O.: sublimis (of a headland), Iu.: levis, a tongue of flame, V.—A hat, helmet, crown: regum apices, H.: summus, the top of the helmet, V.: hi…

aphractus.definition: aphractus ī, f, a)/fraktos (uncovered), a ship without a deck, open boat.

apicatus.definition: apicātus adj. apex, wearing a flamen's cap: Dialis, O.

apis.definition: 'apis is (gen plur. apium, later apum), f a bee: apis aculeus: examen apum, L.: melliferae, O.: Calabrae, H.: parcae, frugal, V.: sedula, busy, O.: insidunt floribus, V.'

apiscor.definition: apīscor aptus, ī AP-, to reach, attain to, get, gain: deorum vitam, T.: maris apiscendi causa: spes apiscendi summi honoris, L.

apium.definition: apium ī, n apis, parsley, with the fragrant leaves, V.: vivax, that long remains green, H.—A parsley wreath was the prize in the Isthmian and Nemean games, Iu.

aplustre.definition: 'aplustre is, n, a)/flaston, an ornament of wood on the stern of a ship: victae triremis, Iu.'

apocleti.definition: apoclētī ōrum, m, a)po/klhtoi, a commission of the Aetolian league, executive committee, L.

apodyterium.definition: apodȳtērium ī, n, a)poduth/rion, an undressing-room (in a bath-house).

apologus.definition: apologus ī, m, a)po/logos, a fable after the manner of Aesop, an apologue.

apoproegmenon.definition: apoproēgmenon ī, n, a)poprohge/non; in philos., that which is to be rejected.

apotheca.definition: apothēca ae, f, a)pothh/kh, a repository, storehouse, magazine, warehouse, C.; esp. for wine, H.

apparate.definition: apparātē (adp-) adv. apparatus, sumptuously: edere et bibere.— Of speech, elaborately, nicely: compositum, Her.

apparatio.definition: apparātiō (adp-) ōnis, f apparo, a preparing: munerum.— Fig., of an orator, preparation.

apparatus1.definition: apparātus (adp-) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of apparo, prepared, ready.—Of persons: ad causam. — Of things, supplied, furnished: domus omnibus apparatior rebus.—Meton., magnificent, splendid, sumptuous: epulae, L.: l…

apparatus2.definition: apparātus (adp-) ūs, m apparo, a preparing, providing, preparation, getting ready: operis: strepere apparatu belli, L.: belli apparatūs. — Apparatus, tools, implements, engines, supplies, material, instruments: ingens…

apparens.definition: appārēns ntis, adj. P. of appareo, visible, manifest: tympana, O.

appareo.definition: appāreō (ad-p-) uī, itūrus, ēre, to appear, come in sight, make an appearance: ille nusquam apparet, T.: Apparent rari nantes, are seen, V.: huic questioni, at this trial: in his (subselliis): de sulcis, O. — Esp., to…

apparitio.definition: appāritiō (adp-) ōnis, f appareo, a serving, service, attendance: longa. — Meton., plur, domestics, servants.

armamaxa.definition: armamaxa ae, f, a(rma/maca, a covered Persian chariot (esp. for women and children), Cu.

armamenta.definition: armāmenta ōrum, n armo, implements, utensils.—Esp., the equipment of a ship, tackle: ancorae reliquaeque armamenta, Cs.: demenda, L.: aptari pinum armamentis, O.

armamentarium.definition: armāmentārium ī, n armamenta, an arsenal, armory: publica: armamentaria caeli, Iu. — Meton., a dockyard: Atheniensibus facere.

armarium.definition: armārium ī, n arma, a closet, chest, safe: in aedibus.

armatura.definition: armātūra ae, f armo, armor, equipment: levis, Cs. — Meton., armed men, troops: levis, light infantry, C., Cs.

armatus1.definition: armātus adj. with sup. P. of armo, armed, equipped, in arms: consuli armatus obstitit: plebes, S.: classes, V.: cohors, Ta.: milia armata quinquagenta, soldiers, Cs.: quasi armatissimi fuerint: facibus, L.: ursi ungui…

armatus2.definition: (armātus ūs), m only abl sing. armo, armor, equipment: haud dispari, L. — Meton., armed men, troops: graviore, L.

armentalis.definition: armentālis e, adj. armentum, of a herd, one of a herd: equa, V.

armentarius.definition: armentārius ī, m armentum, a herdsman, neatherd: Afer, V.

armentum.definition: armentum ī, n aro, cattle for ploughing.— In gen., neat cattle, horned cattle, oxen: greges armentorum reliquique pecoris: bos armenta (sequitur): bucera, O.: armentum aegrotat in agris, H. — Meton., a drove, herd, of…

armifer.definition: 'armifer era, erum, adj. arma + FER-, armsbearing, armed, warlike: Minerva, O.: Leleges, O.'

armiger.definition: armiger erī, m arma + GES-, one who bears arms (late), Cu. — An armor-bearer, shield-bearer (poet.): regis, O.: Iovis, i. e. aquila, V.

armigera.definition: armigera ae, f armiger, a female armorbearer, O.

armilla.definition: 'armilla ae, f armus, a bracelet, armlet, armsing: aureae, L.'

armillatus.definition: armillātus adj. armilla, decked with bracelets: canes. Pr.

armipotens.definition: armipotēns entis, adj. arma + potens, powerful in arms, valiant, warlike: Mars, V.

armisonus.definition: 'armisonus adj. arma + SON-, resounding with arms: Pallas, V.'

armo.definition: armō āvī, ātus, āre arma, to furnish with weapons, arm, equip: multitudinem: milites, Cs.: ut quemque casus armaverat, S.: manū s armat sparus, V.: in dominos armari: in proelia fratres, V.: Archilochum rabies armavit…

armus.definition: armus ī, m 1 AR-, the shoulder: ex umeris armi fiunt, O.: leporis, H.: equi fodere calcaribus armos, the side, V.: hasta per armos Acta, the upper arm, V.

aro.definition: arō āvī, ātus, āre 2 AR-, to plough, till: terram: in fundo, T.: piger optat arare caballus (i. e. rather than carry a rider), H. — Prov.: arare litus, to waste labor, O. — In gen., to cultivate: quae homines arant, n…

arrabo.definition: arrabō ōnis, m, a)rrabw/n, earnest-money, a pledge, security: relicta arraboni, as security, T.

arrepo.definition: arrēpō, arrīdeō, arrogō etc., see adr-.

ars.definition: ars artis, f 1 AR-, practical skill: manus et ars: arte laboratae vestes, V. — Esp., skill in a special pursuit, a profession, business, art: musica, poetry, T.: magica, V.: (artes) militares et imperatoriae, L.: civi…

arte.definition: artē adv. with comp. and sup. artus, closely, fast, firmly: continere alqd, Cs.: aciem statuere, S.: tigna artius inligata, Cs.: quam artissime ire, S. — Fig.: dormire, soundly: alqm colere, i. e. stingily, S.

arteria.definition: artēria ae, f, a)rthri/a, the windpipe. — An artery.

articulatim.definition: articulātim adv. articulus, piecemeal, Poet. ap. C. — Distinctly, in clear sequence: dici.

articulus.definition: articulus ī, m dim. 2 artus. a joint, knuckle: crura sine articulis, Cs.: quo iungitur capiti cervix, L.: sarmentorum. — Esp., plur, the fingers: labella abstergere articulis, Ct.—Fig., of discourse, a part, member. —…

artifex.definition: artifex icis, m and f ars + FAC-, a master of an art, professional man, artist, artificer (used of a sculptor, musician, actor, etc.): artifices improbi, i. e. quacks, L.: dicendi, an orator: morbi, healer, Tb.—A make…

artificiose.definition: artificiōsē adv. with comp. and sup. artificiosus, skilfully, artistically, in an orderly manner: dicere: id artificiousius efficere: artificiosissime facere, Her.

artificiosus.definition: artificiōsus adj. with comp. and sup. artificium, full of skill, skilful, artistic: rhetores artificiosissimi. — Skilfully wrought, artistic: opus: est artificiosius (with inf.), Her.—Artificial: genera divinandi: mem…

artificium.definition: artificium ī, n artifex, a profession, trade, employment, art: tenue: opera atque artificia, Cs. —Theory, system: de iure.—Skill, knowledge, ingenuity: singulare: gubernatoris, Cs.—Art, craft, cunning, artifice, trick…

arto.definition: artō āvī, ātus, āre 1 artus, to contract, straiten: artato freno, Tb.: in honoribus omnia artata, L.

artolaganus.definition: artolaganus ī, m, a)rtola/ganon, a kind of cake.

artopta.definition: artopta ae, f, a)rto/pths, a breadpan, Iu.

artus1.definition: artus (not arctus), adj. with comp. and sup. 1 AR-, close, strait, narrow, confined, short: laquei: saltus, L.: compages, V.: nexus, O.: toga, narrow, H.: convivia, i. e. crowded, H.: artiores silvae, dense, Cs.: cust…

artus2.definition: artūs uum, m plur. 1 AR-, joints: digitorum: dolor artuum, gout.— Meton., the limbs: artubus omnibus: arsuri, i. e. the body, O.: per artūs Sudor iit, V.: singulos artūs, each limb, Ta.: animā seducere artūs, V.

arula.definition: ārula ae, f dim. ara, a small altar.

arvina.definition: arvīna ae, f grease, fat, lard: pinguis, V.

arvum.definition: arvum ī, n arvus, an arable field, cultivated land, field, ploughed land, glebe: optima, V.: arvo studere, S.: fundus Arvo pascat erum, H.: fertilia, L. — Plur, fields, plains, country, regions: Sicula, V.: Quā rigat …

arx.definition: arx arcis (plur. only nom. and acc.), f ARC-, a castle, citadel, fortress, stronghold: (montem) murus arcem efficit, Cs.: munire arcem: arcem tradunt, N.: hostium, L. — In Rome, prop., the southwest summit of the Capi…

as.definition: ās assis, m 2 AC-, one, a whole, unity; hence (late), ex asse heres, of the entire estate. — Esp., the unit of money, orig. one pound of copper; reduced by depreciations to half an ounce; a penny: assem dare: vilis, H…

ascendo.definition: ascendō (adsc-) scendī, scēnsus, ere ad + scando, to mount, climb, ascend, scale, go up: in equum: in caelum: ad Gitanas, L.: Delphos, to Delphi, L.: navem, T.: iugum montis, Cs.: illuc, O.: si mons erat ascendendus, …

ascensio.definition: ascēnsiō (ad-sc-) ōnis, f ascendo, a rising. —Fig. (once): oratorum, progress.

ascensus2.definition: ascēnsus (adsc-) ūs, m ascendo, a climbing, ascent: primos prohibere ascensu, Cs.: difficilis, L.: mollioris ascensūs via, L.: fastigia Ascensu supero, V.—Fig., a rising: ad civitatem, to citizenship.—A way up, approa…

ascio.definition: asciō (ad-sciō) —, —, īre, to receive, adopt, select: socios, V.: centurionem, Ta.

ascisco.definition: ascīscō (ad-sc-) scīvī, scītus, ere, to take to oneself, adopt, accept: leges: aliā (civitate) ascitā, by accepting citizenship elsewhere, N.: si non esset (civis), asciscendum fuisse, ought to be made one: socios sib…

ascitus.definition: ascītus (ad-sc-) adj. P. of ascisco, adopted, foreign, assumed: milites, Cu.: lepor, N.

ascribo.definition: ascrībō (ad-scr-) īpsī, īptus, ere ad + scribo, to write in addition, add: ad extremum alquid: in lege, ‘si quid,’ etc.: nomini regis titulum, Cu. — To enroll, enlist, enter in a list: ascriptus Heracleensis: Puteolos…

ascripticius.definition: ascrīptīcius (ad-scr-) adj. ascribo, received by enrolment (once): cives.

ascriptio.definition: ascrīptiō (ad-scr-) ōnis, f ascribo, an addition in writing, C.

ascriptor.definition: ascrīptor (ad-scr-) ōris, m ascribo, one who adds his name, a supporter: legis: tuus.

asella.definition: 'asella ae, f dim. asina, a small she-ass: turpis, O.'

asellus.definition: asellus ī, m dim. asinus, a little ass, ass's colt: tardus, V.: onustus auro.

asilus.definition: asīlus ī, m a gad-fly, horse-fly, V.

asinus.definition: asinus ī, m an ass, C., L.—Fig., an ass, blockhead, dolt: germanus.

asotus.definition: asōtus ī, m, a)/swtos, a libertine.

asparagus.definition: asparagus ī, m, a)spa/ragos, asparagus, Iu.

aspecto.definition: aspectō (adsp-) āvī, ātus, āre, intens. aspicio, to look at attentively, gaze upon: me, T.: stabula, V. — Of places, to look towards, overlook: collis adspectat arces, V.—Fig., to heed: iussa, Ta.

aspectus2.definition: aspectus (adsp-) ūs (dat. aspectū, V.), m aspicio, a seeing, looking at, sight, view, glance, look: uno aspectu intueri eos: situs praeclarus ad aspectum: aspectum amittere, sight: civium: in aspectu populi positum: t…

aspello.definition: aspellō (abs-) —, —, ere abs + pello, to drive away: ab hac me, T.: a leto numine aspellor, Att. ap. C.

asper.definition: asper era, erum (poet., abl plur. aspris, V.), adj. with comp. and sup. ab + spes, without hope, adverse, calamitous, troublesome, cruel, perilous: tempora: oppugnatio, Cs.: mala res, spes multo asperior, S.: venatus,…

aspere.definition: asperē adv. with comp. and sup. asper, harshly, severely, sternly: in homines invehi: asperius scribere: ius dicere, L.: asperrime loqui, harshly. — Coarsely: vestitus.

aspergo1.definition: aspergō (ads-) ersī, ersus, ere ad + spargo, to scatter, strew upon, sprinkle, spatter over: guttam bulbo: pecori virus, V. — To sprinkle with, besprinkle, bespatter, bedew: aram sanguine: sanguine mensas, O.—Fig., to…

aspergo2.definition: aspergō (adsp-, -argō) inis, f 1 aspergo, a sprinkling, besprinkling: aquarum, O.: sanguis aspergine tinxerat herbas, O. — That which is sprinkled, drops: salsā spumant aspargine, spray, V.: caedis, the sprinkled bloo…

asperitas.definition: asperitās ātis, f asper, unevenness, roughness: viarum: locorum, S.: omnis asperitates supervadere, the obstacles, S.: soni, harshness, Ta.: frigorum, severity, Ta.—Fig., roughness, harshness, severity, fierceness, co…

aspernatio.definition: āspernātiō ōnis, f aspernor, disdain, contempt: rationis.

aspernor.definition: āspernor ātus, ārī, dep. ab + spernor, to disdain, reject, despise: familiam, T.: vos animo: consilia, L.: voluptatem ratione: velut diis aspernantibus placamina irae, L.: furorem a suis aris: alqm militiae dare, refu…

aspero.definition: asperō āvī, ātus, āre asper, to make rough: aquilonibus undas, V.: sagittas ossibus, point, Ta.: pugionem saxo, to whet, Ta.—Fig., to excite, exasperate: hunc in saevitiam, Ta.: iram, Ta.

aspersio.definition: aspersiō ōnis, f 1 aspergo, a sprinkling: aquae.—Of colors on a tablet: fortuita.

aspicio.definition: aspiciō (ad-sp-) ēxī, ectus, ere ad + specio, to look at, look upon, behold, look: ilico, T.: potestas aspiciendi: inter sese, one another: Eius formam, T.: eorum forum, L.: nos, V.: alqm in acie, to face, N.: nec ser…

aspiratio.definition: aspīrātiō (ads-) ōnis, f aspiro, a breathing on, blowing upon: aëris.—Fig., a rough breathing, aspirate. — Exhalation, evaporation: terrarum.— Influence: caeli.

aspiro.definition: aspīrō (ad-sp-) āvī, ātus, āre ad + spiro, to breathe at, blow upon: adspirant aurae in noctem, freshen, V.: pulmones aspirantes, exhaling. — Poet.: ventos eunti, sends favorable breezes, V.: dictis amorem, imparts, V…

aspis.definition: aspis idis, f an asp, viper.

asportatio.definition: asportātiō ōnis, f asporto, a carrying away (once): signorum.

asporto.definition: asportō (abs-p-) āvī, ātus abs + porto, to carry away, carry off, transport, remove: (simulacrum) e signo: ex Siciliā litteras: sua omnia Salamina, N.: (vehiculis) regum res, L.: ad virum uxorem, L.: hinc comitem Creü…

aspreta.definition: asprēta ōrum, n asper, rough places, L.

assa1.definition: āssa ae, f assus, sc. nutrix, a dry nurse, Iu.

assa2.definition: āssa ōrum, n plur., see assus.

asse-.definition: as-se- in words compounded with ad, see ad-se-.

asser.definition: 'asser eris, m ad + 2 sero, a stake, post: cuspidibus praefixi, Cs.: longi, L.'

assi.definition: as-si-, as-su- in compounds of ad, see ad-s-.

assus.definition: āssus adj. for arsus; 3 AR-, roasted: mergi, H. — As subst n., a roast, roast meat: vitulinum. —Plur., H.—Hence, sol, a basking in the sun without anointing.

ast.definition: ast conj., older and poet. for at.

asterno.definition: asternō (ad-st-) —, —, ere ad + sterno, to strew on (once): adsternuntur sepulcro, throw themselves down upon, O.

astipulator.definition: astipulātor (ads-) ōris, m astipulor.—In law, an associate in accepting a verbal contract.— Hence, an assistant, helper (in a trial).— In gen., a follower (in opinion): eorum (Stoicorum).

astipulor.definition: astipulor (ad-st-) ātus, ārī ad + stipulor. — In law, to join the principal, in accepting a verbal contract.—Hence, fig., to agree with, humor: consuli, L.

astiti.definition: astitī.I. Perf. of adsisto.—II. Perf. of asto.

astituo.definition: astituō (ads-) uī, ūtus, ere ad + statuo, to place, station: reum ad lectum, Her.

asto.definition: a-stō (ads-) itī, —, āre ad + sto, to stand at, take place near: accessi, astiti, stood by, T.: astat echinus, is at hand, H.: portis, V.: hic, T.: procul, O.: sedibus, O.: ad Achillis tumulum: in conspectu meo: ante …

astrepo.definition: astrepō (ad-st-) —, —, ere, to make a noise at, resound in response: adstrepebat volgus, Ta.— To assent loudly, applaud: clamore, Ta.: haec dicenti, Ta.: eadem, approve loudly, Ta.

astricte.definition: astrictē adv. astrictus, rigidly, by strict metrical rules: numerosa oratio.

astrictus.definition: astrictus adj. with comp. P. of astringo, drawn together, narrow: limen, O.—Fig., sparing, parsimonious: pater, Pr.: auctor, Ta. — Of language, narrow, concise, compact: verborum comprehensio: eloquentia: numeris astr…

astringo.definition: astringō (ad-st-) inxī, ictus, ere, to bind on, tie fast, fasten to, bind up: ad statuam astrictus: vincula, O.: hederā adstringitur ilex, twined with, H.: cortex astrictus pice, fastened, H.: Cervice adstrictā, with …

astrologia.definition: astrologia ae, f, a)strologi/a, the science of the heavenly bodies, astronomy.

astrologus.definition: astrologus ī, m, a)strolo/gos, an astronomer: novus.—An astrologer, C., Iu.

astrum.definition: astrum ī, n, a)/stron, a heavenly body, star, constellation: astri reditus: Caesaris, the comet of B.C. 43, V.: natale, H.—Plur, the stars, sky, heaven: oculos sub astra tenebat, fixed on the sky, V.: nox caelum spars…

astruo.definition: astruō (ad-st-) ūxī, ūctus, ere ad + struo, to build in addition, add to (a structure): super contignationem, quantum ... (tantum) adstruxerunt, Cs. — To add, confer besides: consulari alquid aliud, Ta.

astu1.definition: astū n indecl., a)/stu, a city, T., C., N.

astupeo.definition: astupeō (ad-st-) —, —, ēre, to be amazed at: sibi, O.

astus.definition: astūs ūs, m 2 AC-, adroitness, craft, cunning.—Usu. abl sing. (of manner): rem tractare, cunningly, T.: Id sollerti furtim astu cepisse, O.: versare dolos, V.: Punico, L.—A stratagem: hostium, Ta.: astūs oppugnationum…

astute.definition: astūtē adv. astutus, craftily, cunningly: ab eā labefactarier, T.: reticere alqd.

astutia.definition: astūtia ae, f astutus, adroitness, shrewdness, craft, cunning: intellegendi, Pac. ap. C.: ad rem, T.: confidens. — Plur, tricks, cunning devices: Hem astutias, T.: tollendae.

astutus.definition: astūtus adj. with comp. astus, wary, shrewd, sagacious, expert: ratio: me astutiorem fingere.— Crafty, cunning, sly, artful: homo: volpes, H.: gens, Ta.

asumbolus.definition: asumbolus (asym-) adj., a)su/mbolos,not contributing, scot-free, T.

asylum.definition: asȳlum ī, n, a)/sulon, a place of refuge, sanctuary, asylum: templa, quae asyla Graeci vocant, L.: in illud asylum confugere: Iunonis, V.: asylum aperire, L.: statuere, Ta.

at.definition: at or (rarely) ast, conj, but (introducing a contrast to what precedes). I. In a transition, but, but on the other hand, but meanwhile: comminus pugnatum est; at Germani impetūs gladiorum exceperunt, Cs.: alius alii v…

atavus.definition: atavus ī, m ad + avus, a grandfather's grandfather, C.—An ancestor, forefather: atavis potens, V.: atavis editus regibus, H.

ater.definition: āter tra, trum, adj. AID-, black, coal-black, gloomy, dark (cf. niger, glossy-black): panis, T.: carbo, T.: alba et atra discernere: noctes, Ta.: tempestas, V.: mare, gloomy, H.: lictores, clothed in black, H.: corvus…

athleta.definition: āthlēta ae, m, a)thlhth/s, a wrestler, athlete, combatant in public games: se exercens in curriculo: athletarum studia, H.

atomus.definition: atomus ī, f, a)/tomos, an indivisible particle, atom.

atque.definition: atque or (only before consonants) ac conj. ad + que, and (like -que, it connects words or thoughts which form a whole, but unlike -que gives prominence rather to what follows, and is rarely repeated). I. Copulative. A…

atqui.definition: at-quī (at-quīn) conj, but somehow, but in any wise, but yet, however, and yet, and nevertheless: modum statuarum haberi nullum placet? atqui habeatur necesse est: mihi numquam venerat in mentem optare ... atqui fuit …

atramentum.definition: ātrāmentum ī, n ater, a black liquid: atramenti effusio: sutorium, blacking for leather (a poisonous liquid).—Ink, writing-ink: labem remittunt Atramenta, H.

atratus.definition: ātrātus adj. ater, clothed in black: plebes, Ta.: equi (of the sun), Pr.

atriensis.definition: ātriēnsis is, m atrium, a steward, chief servant.

atriolum.definition: ātriolum ī, n dim. atrium, a small hall, antechamber.

atrium.definition: ātrium ī, n AID-, a room which contains the hearth, fore-court, hall, principal room, H.—Plur., of one room (poet.): longa, V.: marmore tecta, O.—In a temple or palace, the main hall: Libertatis: regium, L.—An auction…

atrocitas.definition: atrōcitās ātis, f atrox, fierceness, harshness, enormity: ipsius facti: sceleris, S.: poenae, L.— Barbarity, severity, rigidity: animi ista tua.

atrociter.definition: atrōciter adv. with comp. and sup. atrox, fiercely, cruelly, harshly, indignantly minitari: agitare rem p., S.: atrocius in alqm saevire, L.: atrocissime agitur.

atrox.definition: atrōx ōcis, adj. with comp. and sup. ater, savage, fierce, wild, cruel, harsh, severe: Tydides, H.: Iuno, V.: odium exercebat atrox, O.: animus Catonis, resolute, H.: odii Agrippina, in hatred, Ta.—Cruel, horrible, vi…

attactus2.definition: attāctus —, m attingo, a touch, contact (only abl sing.): Volvitur attactu nullo, V., O.

attagen.definition: attagēn ēnis, m, a)ttagh/n, the heath-cock, H.

attat.definition: attāt (ātāt) interj. of surprise, So! hey-day, T.

attegia.definition: 'attegia ae, f a hut: Maurorum, Iu.'

attemperate.definition: attemperātē (adt-) adv. ad + tempero, opportunely, in the nick of time (once): evenit, T.

attendo.definition: attendō (adt-) tendī, tentus, ere ad + tendo, to stretch toward, direct.—With animum, give attention, attend to, consider, give heed: cum animum attenderis, on careful observation: animos ad ea: quid velim, T.: sermo …

attente.definition: attentē (adt-) adv. with comp. and sup. attentus, carefully, considerately, heedfully: officia fungi, T.: audire: attentius auditum: attentissime audiri.

attentio.definition: attentiō ōnis, f attendo, application, attentiveness: animi.

attentus.definition: attentus (adt-) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of attendo, attentive, intent, engaged: animus in spe, T.: Caesaris auris, H.: iudex: me attentissimis animis auditis: attentissima cogitatio.—Intent on, striving after, car…

attenuate.definition: attenuātē (adt-) adv. attenuatus, of style, dryly, without ornament: dicere.

attenuatio.definition: attenuātiō (adt-) ōnis, f a lessening: suspitionis, Her.

attenuatus.definition: attenuātus (adt-) adj. with sup. P. of attenuo, enfeebled, weak: amore, O.: fortuna attenuatissima, Her.—Of discourse, thin, dry: oratio.

attenuo.definition: attenuō (adt-) āvī, ātus, āre ad + tenuo, to make thin, attenuate, lessen, diminish: iuvenum corpora, O.: sortes attenuatae, the tablets had diminished (a sign of adversity), L.—Fig., to reduce, impair, lessen, dimini…

attero.definition: atterō (adt-) trīvī (atterui, Tb.), trītus, ere ad + tero, to rub against, rub away, wear: attritas harenas, O.: herbas, to trample, V.: Cerberus atterens Caudam, i. e. fawning, H. — Fig., to destroy, waste, impair, i…

attestor.definition: attestor (adt-) —, ārī ad + testor, to prove, confirm: hoc, Ph.

attexo.definition: attexō (adt-) —, textus, ere ad + texo, to weave to, join closely: loricae ex cratibus attexuntur, Cs.: barbarorum agris attexta ora.

attice.definition: atticē adv. Atticus, in the Attic style.

attineo.definition: attineō (adt-) tinuī, —, ēre. I. Trans, to hold fast, detain, delay: quam attinendi dominatūs sient, how retained, T. ap. C.: Romanos spe pacis, S.: dextram vi, Ta.—II. Intrans, to stretch, reach: Scythae ad Tanain at…

attingo.definition: attingō (adt-) tigī, tāctus, ere ad + tango, to touch, come in contact with: prius quam aries murum attigisset, Cs.: telas putris, to handle, V.: Maenalon, set foot on, O.: mento aquam: pedibus terram, N.—To touch, st…

attollo.definition: attollō (adt-) —, —, ere ad + tollo, to lift up, raise up, raise, elevate: natum, O.: pallium (i. e. accingere), T.: fracto crure planum, H.: amicum ab humo, V.: oculos humo, O.: oculos contra, i. e. look in the face,…

attondeo.definition: attondeō (adt-) tondī, tōnsus, ēre ad + tondeo, to shave, shear: vitem, to prune, V.: virgulta, to crop, V.—Fig.: laus attonsa, depreciated (poet.).

attonitus.definition: attonitus (adt-) adj. P. of attono, thunderstruck, stunned, astounded: magna pars, struck with terror, L.: animi, V.: talibus visis, V.: turbine rerum, O.: miraculo, L.: domus, awe-struck, V.: voltūs, Ta. — Inspired, …

attono.definition: attonō (adt-) uī, itus, āre, to thunder at, stun, terrify: mentes, O.: Attonitus est committi potuisse nefas, O.

attorqueo.definition: attorqueō (adt-) —, —, ēre ad + torqueo, to hurl upwards: iaculum, V.
